Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Zhang Wei 張偉 comments: Employing men and dispensing rewards and punishments are indeed the fundamental structure and essential pivot of governance. You are able to analyze the various sayings, extol the far-reaching plans and instructions of our Sacred Ancestor, and seek the root in the mind. Detailed, rich, and well-structured, it should be recorded as a model.

Examiner Instructor Tian Younian 田有年 comments: It does not indulge in thorny obscurity, yet its arguments flow smoothly and coherently; it is also a composition that values fundamental structure and essential points.

Examiner Subprefecturalwandering Instructor [Director of Studies] Su Yanlong 蘇延龍 comments: With lofty insight and far-reaching purport, it earnestly takes emulating the Ancestor and nourishing the mind as the plan for sacred governance, showing loyal and forthright counsel.

Now, the duty of a ruler of men is one, while his handles of authority are two. When his duty is not thrown into disorder, this is called having fundamental structure (ti 體); when his handles are not relaxed, this is called having the essential pivot (yao 要). Why is this? In relation to the realm, the ruler of men is the one who unifies and directs it, not one who is unified and directed by it. Therefore, his duty is simply called employing men. By causing the realm to divide offices and keep to their charges, everyone performs his work on behalf of the sovereign above, and the utility of all talents responds like an echo. He is the one who guides and controls it, not one who is guided and controlled by it. Therefore, his handles of authority are called rewarding merit and punishing offenses. By causing…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天下象指而趨則人人競業於下而庶理
之詳輻湊矣明主者不以已為天下用而
能立其體以用天下已不詳於天下而能
操其要以天下為之詳一人而兼聽天下
有餘日而不足於治者非遵是之故哉蓋
古今談主術者往往稱有體有要乃其咸
時採事人人殊指矣較然揭而著之
宜莫如漢戴德之記禮焉以為古之御政
以治天下者天子三公合以執六官惟其
===
所引而之而國以治安和平成定御政之
體也是言體在於任人矣又以為古者天
子以德行能功論吏論吏而法行事治而
功成季冬正法孟春論吏治國之要也是
言要在於賞罰矣德蓋祖孔子六官六轡
之說而演周官月令之義耳請略陳周事
而稽諸孔子昔文王之造周也庸庸祇祇
威威以顯示民斯可以想見其任人之體
賞罰之要焉故孔子稱之曰審此三者而
punctuated: 天下象指而趨，則人人競業於下，而庶理之詳輻湊矣。明主者，不以已為天下用，而能立其體以用天下；已不詳於天下，而能操其要以天下為之詳。一人而兼聽天下，有餘日而不足於治者，非遵是之故哉？蓋古今談主術者，往往稱有體有要，乃其咸時採事，人人殊指矣。較然揭而著之，宜莫如漢戴德之《記禮》焉。以為古之御政以治天下者，天子、三公合以執六官，惟其所引而之，而國以治安和平成定，御政之體也。是言體在於任人矣。又以為古者天子以德行能功論吏，論吏而法行，事治而功成，季冬正法，孟春論吏，治國之要也。是言要在於賞罰矣。德蓋祖孔子六官六轡之說，而演《周官》、《月令》之義耳。請略陳周事而稽諸孔子。昔文王之造周也，庸庸、祇祇、威威，以顯示民，斯可以想見其任人之體、賞罰之要焉。故孔子稱之曰：「審此三者，而
translation_en: … the empire follow his pointers and hasten forward, then everyone below will strive diligently at their duties, and all the minute details of administration will converge like spokes at a hub. An enlightened ruler does not let himself be used by the empire, but is able to establish his fundamental principle to make use of the empire; he does not attend to every detail in the empire himself, but is able to grasp the essentials so that the empire attends to the details for him. When a single man listens to the affairs of the entire empire, having spare time while never falling short in governance, is it not because he follows this way? Indeed, those from ancient to modern times who discuss the art of rulership often speak of having a fundamental principle and having essentials, yet in responding to their times [?] and selecting affairs to discuss, each person points in a different direction. For clearly setting these forth and making them manifest, none can match Dai De 戴德 of the Han in his Record of Rites (Ji li). He held that among the ancients who drove the chariot of government to rule the empire, the Son of Heaven and the Three Dukes joined together to hold the reins of the Six Offices; wherever they drew them, there they went, and thus the state achieved order, security, harmony, and peace—this is the fundamental principle of driving the chariot of government. This means that the fundamental principle lies in employing men. He further held that in antiquity the Son of Heaven evaluated officials by their moral conduct, ability, and merit; when officials were evaluated, the laws were carried out, affairs were well-governed, and achievements were completed; rectifying the laws in the last month of winter and evaluating officials in the first month of spring—this is the essential of governing the state. This means that the essentials lie in rewards and punishments. Dai De was in fact following Confucius's doctrine of the Six Offices as the six reins, while elaborating the meaning of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan) and the Monthly Ordinances (Yueling). Allow me to briefly set forth the affairs of the Zhou and verify them against Confucius. In the past, when King Wen 文王 founded the Zhou, he employed the employable, respected the respectable, and awed those who deserved awe, thereby manifestly displaying this to the people. From this one can envision his fundamental principle of employing men and his essentials of rewards and punishments. Therefore Confucius praised him, saying: "To carefully attend to these three things and yet…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國不興未之有也文王不勞而治則詩人
頌其寧洎成王親政周公作立政以陳規
又拳拳言文王罔兼於有司牧夫之事惟
克知三宅灼見三俊取其用命違命者而
訓勑之云爾成王法之肴牖不徹於前鐘
鼓不解於懸而六服承德其效如此標季
闇於主術其佚豫不恤國者無論即圖治
勵精而不得夫體要硜硜乎以身勞於天
下而終鮮功焉若秦始皇帝量書日夜有
程魏明帝欲按尚書事隋文帝臨朝至日
昃而滋以害治此杜黃裳所爲慨嘆而認
認引以爲誡也遡周而後太平之治綦於
我
===
明
太祖高皇帝天挺聖神躬提三尺盪乾坤之墋
黷開日月於鴻濛郁乎煥哉載在
聖政記諸書者不啻軼成周之隆已愚間嘗仰
窺
punctuated: 國不興，未之有也。」文王不勞而治，則詩人頌其寧。洎成王親政，周公作《立政》以陳規，又拳拳言文王罔兼於有司牧夫之事，惟克知三宅，灼見三俊，取其用命違命者而訓勑之云爾。成王法之，肴牖不徹於前，鐘鼓不解於懸，而六服承德，其效如此。標季闇於主術，其佚豫不恤國者無論，即圖治勵精而不得夫體要，硜硜乎以身勞於天下而終鮮功焉。若秦始皇帝量書日夜有程，魏明帝欲按尚書事，隋文帝臨朝至日昃，而滋以害治，此杜黃裳所爲慨嘆而認認引以爲誡也。遡周而後，太平之治綦於我明。太祖高皇帝天挺聖神，躬提三尺，盪乾坤之墋黷，開日月於鴻濛。郁乎煥哉！載在《聖政記》諸書者，不啻軼成周之隆已。愚間嘗仰窺
translation_en:
…and yet the state did not flourish—there has never been such a case." King Wen (Wen Wang 文王) achieved order without toil, and the poets praised his tranquility. When King Cheng (Cheng Wang 成王) assumed personal rule, the Duke of Zhou (Zhou Gong 周公) composed the "Establishment of Government" (Lizheng 立政) to present guidelines, earnestly stating that King Wen did not concurrently meddle in the affairs of the functionaries and pastors, but only truly knew the incumbents of the three high positions and clearly perceived the men of the three grades of outstanding talent, taking those who obeyed or disobeyed orders and instructing or reprimanding them—and that was all. King Cheng emulated this: meats and vessels [?] were not cleared from before him, bells and drums were not taken down from their stands, and yet the six domains submitted to his virtue. Such was its efficacy.

In later, declining ages [?], rulers were ignorant of the art of sovereignty. Setting aside those who indulged in ease and pleasure without regard for the state, even those who sought good governance and roused their spirits, yet failed to grasp the fundamental structure and essential pivot, obstinately wearied themselves in the affairs of the realm and ultimately achieved little success. For example, the First Emperor of Qin (Qin Shihuangdi 秦始皇帝) weighed documents by a set quota day and night; Emperor Ming of Wei (Wei Mingdi 魏明帝) wished to personally inspect the affairs of the Imperial Secretariat; and Emperor Wen of Sui (Sui Wendi 隋文帝) held court until the sun declined—all of which only increasingly harmed good governance. This is what Du Huangshang 杜黃裳 sighed over and anxiously [?] cited as a warning.

Tracing back from the Zhou dynasty onward, the governance of great peace reached its culmination in our Ming dynasty. Grand Progenitor Emperor Gao (Taizu Gaohuangdi 太祖高皇帝), endowed by Heaven with sagely divinity, personally wielded a three-foot sword, cleansing the defilement of heaven and earth and opening up the sun and moon amid primordial chaos. How richly flourishing and resplendent! What is recorded in the Record of Sacred Governance (Shengzheng ji 聖政記) and other books not only surpasses the prosperity of the accomplished Zhou. I have at times humbly looked up to glimpse…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
規摹之大略蓋在先立其體以統運天下焉
獨操其要以導制天下焉觀夫羣雄逐鹿
之秋
聖祖之闢草昧而經營之也
諭許琰曰予思英賢有如饑渴方當廣攬博
收共成康濟其統運天下之體可見於此矣
若達若遇春若文忠輩仗鉞以宣威若基
若安若濂輩持籌而贊晝得人之盛太常
則紀之追後
===
訪遺逸與孝廉開
制舉歲歲以弓旌輿軨旁求於天下而才者
賢者朝上公車暮
召而對焉簡材以試之官辨官而任之事是故
合天人調四時者四輔也衡鑑平明者冢
卿也培邦本足國用者司徒也和上下治
神人者宗伯也山川險易夷番歸附者司
馬也體欽恤振紀綱者司寇憲臺也諸如
此類不可殫述夫以
punctuated: 規摹之大略，蓋在先立其體以統運天下焉，獨操其要以導制天下焉。觀夫羣雄逐鹿之秋，聖祖之闢草昧而經營之也，諭許琰曰：「予思英賢，有如饑渴，方當廣攬博收，共成康濟。」其統運天下之體，可見於此矣。若達、若遇春、若文忠輩，仗鉞以宣威；若基、若安、若濂輩，持籌而贊晝。得人之盛，太常則紀之。追後訪遺逸，與孝廉，開制舉，歲歲以弓旌輿軨旁求於天下。而才者、賢者，朝上公車，暮召而對焉。簡材以試之官，辨官而任之事。是故合天人、調四時者，四輔也；衡鑑平明者，冢卿也；培邦本、足國用者，司徒也；和上下、治神人者，宗伯也；山川險易、夷番歸附者，司馬也；體欽恤、振紀綱者，司寇、憲臺也。諸如此類，不可殫述。夫以
translation_en: … the general outline of his grand design: it lay in first establishing the fundamental body of governance so as to comprehensively direct the realm, and in solely grasping the essential pivot so as to guide and control the realm. Consider that time when rival warlords were contending for the throne, as the Sacred Ancestor opened up a world in primeval chaos and set it in order. He instructed Xu Yan 許琰, saying: "I long for outstanding and worthy men as if hungry and thirsty; right now we must gather and recruit them broadly, so as to achieve peace and deliverance together." The fundamental principle by which he comprehensively directed the realm can be seen in this. Men such as [Xu] Da 徐達, [Chang] Yuchun 常遇春, and [Li] Wenzhong 李文忠 wielded battle-axes to project martial might; men such as [Liu] Ji 劉基, [陶] An 陶安, and [Song] Lian 宋濂 held the counting rods to assist in planning [read 畫 for 晝?]. The flourishing abundance of talent he obtained was recorded by the Chamberlain for Ceremonials (taichang). Later on [read 迨 for 追?], he sought out recluse talents, promoted the Filial and Incorrupt (xiaolian), and instituted the civil service examinations by imperial decree, year after year sending out bows, banners, and carriages to search far and wide across the empire. As for the talented and the worthy, if they arrived by official carriage in the morning, by evening they were summoned for an audience. He selected men of ability to test them in office, and distinguished among offices to entrust them with responsibilities. Therefore, those who harmonized Heaven and man and regulated the four seasons were the Four Assistants (sifu); the one whose balance and mirror of judgment were fair and clear was the Minister of Personnel (zhongqing); the one who nurtured the root of the state and sufficed for national expenditure was the Minister of Revenue (situ); the one who brought harmony between superiors and inferiors and governed spirits and men was the Minister of Rites (zongbo); the one who oversaw the strategic terrain of mountains and rivers and the submission of foreign tribes was the Minister of War (sima); and those who embodied reverent compassion in punishment and upheld the laws and discipline were the Minister of Justice (sikou) and the Censorate (xiantai). Examples of this sort are too numerous to recount in full. Now, with …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聖祖之神智豈不欲遐燭乎萬方而獨審愼於
任人如此其不自用者乃其所以用歟觀
夫衆傑攀龍之日
聖祖之提衡紲而駕馭之也
諭范祖幹曰吾號令賞罰一有不平何以服
衆其導制天下之要可見於此矣若和若永
忠若勝輩封命不蓋愆若茂若通源若顯
輩譴辭不忘勸勸沮之章盟府則載之迨
後歲考課稽名實察毀譽時時以軒冕鈇
鉞砥礪乎天下而功者罪者暮聞
===
斧扆朝
臨而斷焉善無微而不錄慝有細而必懲是故
在職公勤而復其家矣啓事一私而逮矣
不受遺金而超遷矣詭脫圄犴而廷訊誅
之矣持法繩姦而被文綺衣鈔璽書醴酒
之勞矣問閭閻疾苦無所對而竄矣諸如
此類未易僂指夫以
聖祖之憂勤豈不欲周知乎百度而獨精嚴於
punctuated: 聖祖之神智，豈不欲遐燭乎萬方，而獨審愼於任人如此，其不自用者，乃其所以用歟？觀夫衆傑攀龍之日，聖祖之提衡紲而駕馭之也，諭范祖幹曰：「吾號令賞罰，一有不平，何以服衆？」其導制天下之要，可見於此矣。若和、若永忠、若勝輩，封命不蓋愆；若茂、若通源、若顯輩，譴辭不忘勸。勸沮之章，盟府則載之。迨後歲考課，稽名實，察毀譽，時時以軒冕、鈇鉞砥礪乎天下。而功者、罪者，暮聞斧扆，朝臨而斷焉。善無微而不錄，慝有細而必懲。是故在職公勤，而復其家矣；啓事一私，而逮矣；不受遺金，而超遷矣；詭脫圄犴，而廷訊誅之矣；持法繩姦，而被文綺、衣、鈔、璽書、醴酒之勞矣；問閭閻疾苦，無所對，而竄矣。諸如此類，未易僂指。夫以聖祖之憂勤，豈不欲周知乎百度，而獨精嚴於
translation_en: … the Sacred Ancestor's divine wisdom, would he not have wished to shine his light far into the ten thousand regions? Yet he was solely so cautious and careful in appointing men; was not his refusal to rely on himself alone the very means by which he exercised his capacity? Consider the days when the multitude of heroes clung to the dragon's scales, and how the Sacred Ancestor held the yoke and reins to drive them. He instructed Fan Zugan 范祖幹, saying: "In my commands, rewards, and punishments, if there is a single instance of unfairness, how can I win the submission of the multitude?" The essential principle by which he guided and controlled the empire can be seen in this. In the cases of men like Tang He 湯和, Liao Yongzhong 廖永忠, and Feng Sheng 馮勝, the patents enfeoffing them did not conceal their faults; in the cases of men like Chang Mao 常茂, Lu Tongyuan 陸通源, and藍/梁顯 [?] Xian 顯, the words reprimanding them did not forget to encourage them. These documents of encouragement and deterrence are recorded in the House of Covenants. Later, he conducted annual evaluations of official performance, verifying names against realities, examining criticisms and praises, and constantly using high carriages and ceremonial caps or executioners' axes to whet and discipline the empire. As for the meritorious and the guilty, if word reached the imperial screen in the evening, he would attend court in the morning and pass judgment. No goodness was too small to be recorded, and no evil was so slight as to escape punishment. For this reason, when someone was public-spirited and diligent in office, his household was exempted from service; when someone showed a single bit of partiality in reporting business, he was arrested; when someone refused a gift of gold, he was given a supernumerary promotion; when someone deceitfully allowed prisoners to escape from jail, he was interrogated at court and executed; when someone upheld the law to restrain the wicked, he was rewarded for his toil with patterned silks, robes, paper money, an imperial letter, and sweet wine; and when someone was asked about the hardships of the common villages and had no reply, he was banished. Cases of this sort cannot easily be counted on one's fingers. Now, with the Sacred Ancestor's anxious diligence, would he not have wished to be thoroughly acquainted with all administrative measures? Yet he was solely so precise and strict in …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
賞功罰罪如此其不自詳者乃其所以詳
歟當斯時也亨屯之際肇起經綸天下庶
務至繁賾矣張文輔嘗奏言不滿旬之間
而封章所白事以三千三百數我
聖祖兼聽之兼炤之而不勞何其易哉體要得
而朝無曠位位無瘝官官無曠忠忠無遺
謀夫是以廓綱恢紘而萬萬禩之
鴻業乃建也代更
十聖歷二百有餘年
===
皇上以叡冲凝寶命赫然纂而光之方
嗣服之初即嘉與賢公卿討論憲章典脩
聖緒蓋於今十年釀化日登而
上春秋日富
綜攬乾綱
躬親裁斷引
聖祖之鴻業而彌熾彌昌於茲乎在矣執事猶
欲倣周公立政之陳而詢所以獻忠於
上愚竊以為
punctuated: 賞功罰罪如此，其不自詳者，乃其所以詳歟？當斯時也，亨屯之際，肇起經綸，天下庶務至繁賾矣。張文輔嘗奏言，不滿旬之間，而封章所白事以三千三百數。我聖祖兼聽之，兼炤之而不勞，何其易哉！體要得，而朝無曠位，位無瘝官，官無曠忠，忠無遺謀。夫是以廓綱恢紘，而萬萬禩之鴻業乃建也。代更十聖，歷二百有餘年，皇上以叡冲凝寶命，赫然纂而光之。方嗣服之初，即嘉與賢公卿討論憲章，典脩聖緒。蓋於今十年，釀化日登，而上春秋日富，綜攬乾綱，躬親裁斷，引聖祖之鴻業而彌熾彌昌，於茲乎在矣。執事猶欲倣周公《立政》之陳，而詢所以獻忠於上，愚竊以為
translation_en: … rewarding merit and punishing crime in this manner? Was it not that what He did not personally attend to in detail was precisely how everything was attended to in detail? At that time, at the juncture of emerging from difficulty into prosperity, when imperial governance was first being established, the myriad affairs of the empire were extraordinarily complex and intricate. Zhang Wenfu 張文輔 once reported in a memorial that in the span of less than ten days, the matters presented in sealed memorials numbered three thousand three hundred. Our Sacred Ancestor listened to them all and illuminated them all without growing weary—how effortless it was! Once the fundamental principles and essentials were grasped, the court had no vacant positions, positions had no neglectful officials, officials had no unfulfilled loyalty, and loyalty left no counsel unoffered. Thus, the greatstays of the state were broadened and expanded, and the grand enterprise for tens of thousands of generations was thereby established. Through the succession of ten Sacred Emperors, spanning more than two hundred years, His Majesty, with sagely youth, has consolidated the precious Mandate, gloriously continuing and magnifying it. Right at the beginning of His succession to the throne, He delighted in discussing the constitutional statutes with worthy grandees and ministers, dutifully cultivating the sacred heritage. Now, for ten years, transformative governance has daily ascended, while His Majesty grows ever richer in years. Gathering the sovereign authority into His own hands and personally making final decisions, the extending of the Sacred Ancestor's grand enterprise so that it grows ever more flourishing and prosperous rests in this very moment. Yet Your Excellency still wishes to emulate the Duke of Zhou's presentation of the Establishment of Government (Lizheng) and inquires into how to offer loyalty to His Majesty. In my humble opinion, …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
今日
聖心之所宜加者惟貴乎脩一職而法
聖祖統運天下之體提二柄而法
聖祖導制天下之要政之委瑣細微者固不必
盡關
宸慮焉夫立政之書大抵規成王勿誤於有司
牧夫之事而言必稱文王若曰此所受於
文王之徽言而文子文孫之法已此矣今
不有
===
聖祖之謨訓在乎蓋
聖祖臨御三十餘年間其覽斷所最重在任人
賞功罰罪三者洋洋
聖謨垂諸琬琰或喻物或評古數矣乃又標大
指於
祖訓首章愚雨恭誦而得其槩焉謂委任重輕
有梁棟栱桷之喻謂材具短長有莫邪騏
驥之喻與夫曰試曰察而戒用舍之姑息
其啓
punctuated: 今日聖心之所宜加者，惟貴乎脩一職而法聖祖統運天下之體，提二柄而法聖祖導制天下之要；政之委瑣細微者，固不必盡關宸慮焉。夫《立政》之書，大抵規成王勿誤於有司牧夫之事，而言必稱文王，若曰此所受於文王之徽言，而文子文孫之法已此矣。今不有聖祖之謨訓在乎？蓋聖祖臨御三十餘年間，其覽斷所最重，在任人、賞功、罰罪三者。洋洋聖謨，垂諸琬琰，或喻物，或評古，數矣；乃又標大指於《祖訓》首章。愚雨恭誦而得其槩焉：謂委任重輕，有梁棟栱桷之喻；謂材具短長，有莫邪騏驥之喻；與夫曰試、曰察，而戒用舍之姑息，其啓
translation_en: … what the sacred mind today ought to apply itself to lies solely in cultivating the one duty and emulating the Sacred Ancestor's fundamental way of governing and moving the realm, and in grasping the two handles and emulating the Sacred Ancestor's essential means of guiding and controlling the realm; as for the trivial and minute details of governance, they certainly need not all occupy the imperial thoughts. Now, the document "Establishment of Government" (Lizheng) generally admonishes King Cheng not to err by interfering in the affairs of ordinary officials and local governors, and in its words it invariably invokes King Wen, as if to say: these are the admirable words received from King Wen, and the model for his accomplished sons and accomplished grandsons goes no further than this. Today, do we not have the counsels and instructions of the Sacred Ancestor before us? Indeed, during the more than thirty years of the Sacred Ancestor's reign, what he valued most in his review and decision of affairs were three things: employing men, rewarding merit, and punishing offenses. Vast and glorious are the sacred counsels, handed down upon fine jade tablets; at times drawing analogies from things, at times evaluating antiquity, they appear repeatedly—and he further set forth their main purport in the opening chapter of the Ancestral Instructions (Zuxun). Having repeatedly [?] and reverently recited them, I have grasped their general outline: speaking of the greater and lesser weight of delegated responsibilities, there is the analogy of ridgepoles, beams, brackets, and rafters; speaking of the strengths and weaknesses of talents and capabilities, there is the analogy of the Moye sword and the Qiji steed; together with his speaking of "testing" and "examining," and his warning against laxity and indulgence in employing and dismissing—how brilliantly clear is his enlightening of…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
後聖以鏡材審官之體何昭粲也謂勿私愛惡
有丁公雍齒權萬紀李仁發魏徵之評謂
勿掩功過有韓信彭越侯君集之評與夫
曰當曰明而著天人之謹畏其啓
後聖以彰善癉惡之要何肅毅也
皇上第考
謨訓之明徵脩覲揚之令軌論官材於重輕長
短之間得人焉而畀其所重如四輔九官
之列不使高司稼夷典樂用違其長四輔
===
冕旒位宁穆然執大象以昭臨之以言試事以
九官之任得人而其下無不得矣
事察功塞險詖請謁之門絕諛佞逢迎之
路使愛惡一出於正承天道順人情程量
其功過而賞罰行焉是故拔舉而不失其
能官施而不失其宜使天下咸仰
上之明決擇不疑於邪正予奪不搖於是非使
天下咸服
上之斷賞一有功而千萬人之無功者奮使天
punctuated:
後聖以鏡材審官之體，何昭粲也！謂勿私愛惡，有丁公、雍齒、權萬紀、李仁發、魏徵之評；謂勿掩功過，有韓信、彭越、侯君集之評；與夫曰當、曰明，而著天人之謹畏，其啓後聖以彰善癉惡之要，何肅毅也！
皇上第考謨訓之明徵，脩覲揚之令軌，論官材於重輕長短之間，得人焉而畀其所重，如四輔、九官之列，不使高司稼、夷典樂，用違其長，四輔冕旒位宁，穆然執大象以昭臨之，以言試事，以九官之任得人，而其下無不得矣。事察功，塞險詖請謁之門，絕諛佞逢迎之路，使愛惡一出於正，承天道，順人情，程量其功過而賞罰行焉。是故拔舉而不失其能，官施而不失其宜，使天下咸仰上之明；決擇不疑於邪正，予奪不搖於是非，使天下咸服上之斷；賞一有功而千萬人之無功者奮，使天
translation_en:
…succeeding sage emperors in the principles of mirroring talent and examining officials—how brilliantly luminous! Regarding not indulging private likes and dislikes, there are his evaluations of Ding Gong 丁公, Yong Chi 雍齒, Quan Wanji 權萬紀, Li Renfa 李仁發, and Wei Zheng 魏徵; regarding not obscuring merits and faults, there are his evaluations of Han Xin 韓信, Peng Yue 彭越, and Hou Junji 侯君集; and furthermore, in speaking of appropriateness and clarity while emphasizing reverent awe before Heaven and man, how solemn and resolute is his instruction to succeeding sage emperors in the essentials of praising the good and punishing the wicked!

Your Majesty need only examine the clear proofs of these counsels and instructions, cultivate the fine path of honoring and extolling them, and assess official talents in terms of their relative weight and strengths and weaknesses. When the right men are found, entrust them with weighty responsibilities, as in the ranks of the Four Assistants and Nine Officials, without making Gao 高 [for棄 Qi?] take charge of agriculture or Yi 夷 [for 夔 Kui?] direct music, which would employ them contrary to their strengths. Once the offices of the Four Assistants and Nine Officials [note: column order in transcription displaces "冕旒位宁穆然執大象以昭臨之以言試事以" before "九官之任得人而其下無不得矣"] have obtained the right men, there will be none below them who are not well chosen. Wearing the imperial crown and seated behind the screen, Your Majesty may then solemnly uphold the Great Image to shine down upon them: testing their deeds by their words and examining their merits by their deeds, blocking the gates of sinister bias and private solicitation, and cutting off the paths of flattery and sycophancy. Cause likes and dislikes to issue entirely from what is upright; comply with the Way of Heaven and accord with human sentiment, measuring their merits and faults so that rewards and punishments are carried out accordingly. Therefore, when promotions and selections do not miss their abilities, and official appointments do not miss what is suitable, all under Heaven will look up to Your Majesty's clarity; when choices do not waver between the crooked and the upright, and granting and deprivation are not shaken regarding right and wrong, all under Heaven will submit to Your Majesty's decisiveness; when rewarding a single person of merit rouses tens of thousands without merit to exert themselves, causing all under…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
下咸歆
上之福罰一有罪而千萬人之無罪者戒使天
下咸慴
上之威如此則百吏勉盡而衆庶不偷賢者貢
其能不肖者畢其力
天子恭已南面拱揖指麾而四海之內莫不平
均莫不治辯矣成王歌雍詠勺之盛寧踰
此哉雖然愚尤進此而有獻焉荀悅之論
政體也曰皇作極臣作輔而司馬光言治
===
要必先以脩心人主欲臣下之宿道鄉方
而已不爲之端治本以建極則人無稟德
之誠而事多具文之弊矣顧其本繫於人
主之一心心弗正則好尚易移而嗜欲萌
起左右近習勢然伺其所嚮而中之不入
於逸豫必入於紛更其鑑於治等耳徒屬
任乎其臣而督責之曰此體要猶之立枉
木而求景之直也詎不悖哉我
聖祖嘗曰君心當謹嗜好不爲物誘如明鏡止
punctuated: 下咸歆上之福；罰一有罪，而千萬人之無罪者戒，使天下咸慴上之威。如此，則百吏勉盡，而衆庶不偷，賢者貢其能，不肖者畢其力。天子恭已南面，拱揖指麾，而四海之內莫不平均，莫不治辯矣。成王歌《雍》詠《勺》之盛，寧踰此哉？雖然，愚尤進此而有獻焉。荀悅之論政體也，曰：「皇作極，臣作輔。」而司馬光言治要，必先以脩心。人主欲臣下之宿道鄉方，而已不爲之端治本以建極，則人無稟德之誠，而事多具文之弊矣。顧其本繫於人主之一心。心弗正，則好尚易移，而嗜欲萌起；左右近習勢然伺其所嚮而中之，不入於逸豫，必入於紛更，其鑑於治等耳。徒屬任乎其臣而督責之，曰：「此體要。」猶之立枉木而求景之直也，詎不悖哉！我聖祖嘗曰：「君心當謹嗜好，不爲物誘，如明鏡止…
translation_en:
…all under Heaven will delight in the Sovereign's blessings; when he punishes a single guilty man, tens of thousands of the innocent will take warning, causing all under Heaven to stand in awe of the Sovereign's majesty. When it is thus, the hundred officials will strive to do their utmost and the common multitude will not be lax; the worthy will contribute their abilities, and the unworthy will exhaust their strength. The Son of Heaven need only hold himself in reverent composure facing south, clasping his hands and gesturing in command, and within the four seas all will be equitable and in well-ordered governance. Even the flourishing age of King Cheng, when the "Yong" was sung and the "Shao" was chanted, how could it surpass this?

Even so, in my foolishness I would go a step further to offer counsel. When Xun Yue 荀悅 discussed the fundamentals of governance, he said: "The sovereign establishes the standard of perfection; the ministers act as his coadjutors." And when Sima Guang 司馬光 spoke of the essentials of governance, he insisted on beginning with cultivating the mind. If a ruler desires his ministers and subordinates to abide in the Way and turn toward righteousness, yet does not himself rectify the root of governance so as to establish the standard of perfection, then men will lack the sincerity of receiving his virtue, and affairs will suffer mostly from the abuse of mere empty formality. Truly, this root is tied to the single mind of the ruler. If his mind is not rectified, his preferences are easily shifted and his desires sprout forth. His close attendants and favorites will inevitably watch the direction of his inclinations to cater to them; if governance does not sink into idle pleasure, it will surely fall into chaotic alterations—the detriment to order [?] is the same in either case. Merely to delegate responsibilities to one's ministers and hold them strictly to account, saying, "This is the essential principle," is just like setting up a crooked piece of wood and demanding a straight shadow—how could that not be perverse! Our Sacred Ancestor once said: "The ruler's mind ought to guard against partialities and desires, not being lured by external things, like a clear mirror and still…"

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不可以鑑照萬物此又脩心建極之體要𠃍
惟
明主幸謹於玆
第二問
賈璵
同考試官訓導蔡〔子周〕批〔敷敭三德之用援古證今不謬〕
不激蓋非徒侈空鑿者取之
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批〔廣摭衆論而披瀝一得深養士也〕
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批〔剷去膚筌究極本旨〕
===
古之人君所以秉全德而臻至治者固必
有剛柔寬猛之用以章翊世之規亦必有
通變化裁之宜以措因時之政蓋治本畫
一固不便於解更而道有張弛誠有難於
膠故此拘方襲陋者方恬愉焉卑爲無甚
高論而
秉靈握圖之聖主所御幄而咨當扆而宵旰
不遑者也試詳言之世道之變江河之日
趨也文質淆焉隆汙異焉縣遠於鴻荒樸
punctuated:
不可以鑑照萬物。」此又脩心建極之體要𠃍。惟明主幸謹於玆。
第二問
賈璵
同考試官訓導蔡〔子周〕批：〔敷敭三德之用，援古證今，不謬〕不激，蓋非徒侈空鑿者。取之。
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批：〔廣摭衆論，而披瀝一得，深養士也。〕
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批：〔剷去膚筌，究極本旨。〕
古之人君所以秉全德而臻至治者，固必有剛柔寬猛之用，以章翊世之規；亦必有通變化裁之宜，以措因時之政。蓋治本畫一，固不便於解更；而道有張弛，誠有難於膠故。此拘方襲陋者方恬愉焉，卑爲無甚高論；而秉靈握圖之聖主，所御幄而咨、當扆而宵旰不遑者也。試詳言之：世道之變，江河之日趨也。文質淆焉，隆汙異焉，縣遠於鴻荒樸…
translation_en:
…still water[?], so that it can reflect all things as in a mirror.” This, again, is the fundamental essence of cultivating the mind and establishing the supreme standard [?]. May the enlightened ruler graciously take heed of this!

Second Question
Jia Yu 賈璵

Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Cai [Zizhou 子周] comments: [He sets forth and expounds the application of the Three Virtues, citing antiquity to verify the present; it is neither erroneous] nor extreme, and clearly not the work of one who merely indulges in empty and forced theories. Selected.
Examiner and Instructor Tian [Younian 有年] comments: [He gathers widely from the arguments of many and pours forth his own insight; he is a scholar of deep cultivation.]
Examiner and Director of Studies Su [Tinglong 廷龍] comments: [He strips away superficial trappings and thoroughly reaches the fundamental purport.]

Whereby the rulers of antiquity held fast to complete virtue and attained consummate governance was assuredly by possessing the application of firmness and gentleness, leniency and severity, so as to manifest the regulations for assisting the world; and also by possessing the appropriateness of flexibly adapting and tailoring, so as to institute policies suited to the times. For although the foundation of governance is uniform and certainly not convenient to loosen or alter, the Way has its tension and relaxation, making it truly difficult to cling stubbornly to old routines. Those who are bound by convention and perpetuate vulgarity remain complacent in this, dismissing things as requiring no lofty theories; yet for a sacred ruler who holds numinous power and grasps the imperial chart, this is that over which he takes counsel in the imperial tent and labors from before dawn until late at night before the throne screen without leisure. Let me speak of it in detail: the transformation of the ways of the world is like great rivers rushing down day by day. Refinement and substance become confused therein; flourishing and decline diverge therein. Far removed from the simple…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
略剎裂於封豕窫窳而中雜沓之以功利
縱橫堙塞汨沒統緒相沿剎而復泰往而
蹇來者何限也箕子衍三德之疇一曰平
康正直二曰剛克三曰柔克夫聖人豈不
願平康至治渾渾噩噩相忘無事哉其不
得不變而異剛柔之用者勢也風會之流
遷下如冶之範金隨所鎔鑄宥無定質泥
之在陶也埏埴亦隨欲焉而未有偏閡者
也故三德曰乂用誠旨哉其言之矣上之
===
如曰剛可明作吾治也惟利用剛焉固有
竭澤削之束濕操之辛螫如蠆而苛密如
秋荼者矣以是爲理不草菅魚肉之乎柔
可敦裕吾治也惟利用柔焉固有髖髀即
折擁腫即廢姦回將䏶公車縣官不具駒
駟者矣以是爲理不黜嫚毀裂之乎今夫
立天之道曰陰與陽陽以舒之而甲拆萌
荄布濩蟬聯陰以慘之而繁林華藥搖落
委脫互根交禪天道也時之所在天且弗
punctuated: 略，剎裂於封豕窫窳，而中雜沓之以功利縱橫，堙塞汨沒，統緒相沿，剎而復，泰往而蹇來者，何限也！箕子衍三德之疇：一曰平康正直，二曰剛克，三曰柔克。夫聖人豈不願平康至治，渾渾噩噩，相忘無事哉？其不得不變而異剛柔之用者，勢也。風會之流遷，下如冶之範金，隨所鎔鑄，宥無定質；泥之在陶也，埏埴亦隨欲焉，而未有偏閡者也。故三德曰「乂用」，誠旨哉其言之矣！上之如曰剛可明作，吾治也惟利用剛焉，固有竭澤削之，束濕操之，辛螫如蠆而苛密如秋荼者矣。以是爲理，不草菅魚肉之乎？柔可敦裕，吾治也惟利用柔焉，固有髖髀即折，擁腫即廢，姦回將䏶，公車縣官不具駒駟者矣。以是爲理，不黜嫚毀裂之乎？今夫立天之道，曰陰與陽。陽以舒之，而甲拆萌荄，布濩蟬聯；陰以慘之，而繁林華藥，搖落委脫。互根交禪，天道也。時之所在，天且弗
translation_en: …simplicity, torn apart by the Giant Boar and the Yayu beast, and in between jumbled together with utilitarian schemes and diplomatic maneuvers, choked and submerged. As the line of succession was passed down, how limitless were the instances of剝 [decay, transcribed as 剎] turning to Recovery (Fu), or Peace (Tai) departing and Obstruction (Jian) arriving! Jizi elaborated the category of the Three Virtues: the first is called peace and uprightness, the second is called overcoming by firmness, and the third is called overcoming by gentleness. Now, how could the sages not wish for the supreme governance of peace and tranquillity, simple and unspoiled, where all forget one another in the absence of incidents? That they had no choice but to change and differentiate the uses of firmness and gentleness was due to the force of circumstances. The shifting currents of customs and eras are, among those below, like metal cast by a founder—following whatever form it is melted and poured into, having no fixed substance [?]; or like clay on the potter's wheel—molded and shaped according to his wishes, without any one-sided obstruction. Therefore, of the Three Virtues it is said they are "used for governance" (yi yong)—how truly profound are those words! If those above say, "Firmness can stimulate action, so in my governance I shall exclusively employ firmness," there will certainly be those who pare the people down as if draining a marsh to catch fish, who handle them as urgently as tying up wet leather, stinging bitterly like scorpions and imposing laws as harsh and dense as autumn weeds. To govern by such means—is it not to treat the people like grass to be cut or fish and flesh to be butchered? Or if they say, "Gentleness can foster generous abundance, so in my governance I shall exclusively employ gentleness," there will certainly be cases where the blade breaks as soon as it meets a hipbone, where what is knotted and swollen is simply abandoned, where the treacherous and perverse grow fat [?], and where the state carriages and the government cannot even outfit a team of four colts. To govern by such means—is it not to invite degradation, insolence, ruin, and fragmentation? Now, what establishes the Way of Heaven is called yin and yang. Yang unfolds things, so that husks split open and buds and roots spread out in continuous succession; yin chills things, so that dense forests and luxuriant blossoms wither, fall, and drop away. Taking root in one another and yielding to one another in turn—such is the Way of Heaven. Where the season leads, even Heaven does not…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
違矣夫剛乾也陽也柔坤也陰也體固懸
殊而用非軏別者故楊中立謂爲政耎厲
威嚴以陽剛聖人所尚而威嚴即陽剛之
發耳周公謂惟克果斷乃罔後艱以乾健
爲治道所先而果斷亦乾健之用耳其與
火烈鮮蹈水弱多溺子產所爲子大叔飭
者均之對柔而論而剛所急也安謂剛可
獨運也乎哉列子謂剛爲常不勝柔爲常
勝蓋祖常樅齒亡舌存之旨耳淮南子謂
===
兵强則滅木强則折蓋襲老子柔弱堅强
之說耳其與豈弟恩宥收電迴霜陸機所
爲平原陳者均之對剛而論而柔不廢也
安謂柔可獨先也乎哉寬猛相濟政是以
和嘗聞之夫子矣讞交濟之義以覬和中
之化吾未見其得也新國輕典亂國重典
平國中典嘗考之周官矣諄權衡之正以
收寧謐之績吾未見其得也不疑愼爲勝
之戒而曰太剛則折太柔則廢其庶乎知
punctuated: 違矣。夫剛，乾也，陽也；柔，坤也，陰也。體固懸殊，而用非軏別者。故楊中立謂：「爲政耎厲威嚴。」以陽剛聖人所尚，而威嚴即陽剛之發耳。周公謂：「惟克果斷，乃罔後艱。」以乾健爲治道所先，而果斷亦乾健之用耳。其與「火烈鮮蹈，水弱多溺」，子產所爲子大叔飭者，均之對柔而論，而剛所急也。安謂剛可獨運也乎哉？列子謂：「剛爲常不勝，柔爲常勝。」蓋祖常樅「齒亡舌存」之旨耳。淮南子謂：「兵强則滅，木强則折。」蓋襲老子柔弱堅强之說耳。其與「豈弟恩宥，收電迴霜」，陸機所爲平原陳者，均之對剛而論，而柔不廢也。安謂柔可獨先也乎哉？「寬猛相濟，政是以和」，嘗聞之夫子矣。讞交濟之義，以覬和中之化，吾未見其得也。「新國輕典，亂國重典，平國中典」，嘗考之《周官》矣。諄權衡之正，以收寧謐之績，吾未見其得也。不疑愼爲勝之戒，而曰：「太剛則折，太柔則廢。」其庶乎知
translation_en: … defy it. Now firmness is Qian (Heaven) and yang; gentleness is Kun (Earth) and yin. Their essences are certainly far apart, yet in application they are not sharply sundered. Thus Yang Zhongli (Yang Shi 楊時) said, "In governing, one should rouse oneself to sternness [?] and majesty," taking yang firmness as what the sages esteemed, and majesty as simply the manifestation of yang firmness. The Duke of Zhou said, "Only by being able to act resolutely will there be no later difficulties," taking the vigor of Qian as the first priority in the way of governance, and resoluteness as simply the application of that vigor of Qian. Along with the saying "Fire is fierce, so few tread upon it; water is weak, so many drown in it," with which Zichan admonished Zi Taishu, these are all discussed by way of contrast with gentleness, showing where firmness is urgently needed. Yet how could anyone say that firmness can be wielded alone? Liezi said, "The firm regularly fails to overcome; the gentle regularly overcomes," which merely follows the purport of Chang Cong's remark that "the teeth perish while the tongue survives." Master Huainan (Huainanzi) said, "When an army is too strong, it is destroyed; when a tree is too stiff, it breaks," which merely borrows Laozi's doctrine of the gentle and weak versus the hard and strong. Along with "affable and merciful pardoning, gathering in the lightning and turning back the frost," which Lu Ji set forth as Marquis of Pingyuan [?], these are all discussed by way of contrast with firmness, showing that gentleness is not to be discarded. Yet how could anyone say that gentleness alone can be put first? "When leniency and severity complement each other, governance thereby becomes harmonious"—this we have heard from the Master (Confucius). If one casts aside [?] the principle of mutual complementarity and yet hopes for the transformation of harmonious equilibrium, I have never seen that succeed. "For a newly established state, use light penalties; for a disorderly state, use heavy penalties; for an orderly state, use moderate penalties"—this we have examined in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan). If one errs from [?] the correctness of this balancing and yet hopes to reap the achievement of peace and tranquility, I have never seen that succeed.雋不疑 (Jun Buyi) offered his warning to Master Sheng (Bao Shengzhi 暴勝之), saying, "What is too firm will break; what is too gentle will fail." He came close indeed to knowing…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
此道矣是道也羹之鹽梅酒之麴櫱孰能
廢之偏重專一政迺攸斁緣此而張弛錯
事也洵其然與三代而上毋贅已漢高祖
以神武蹙秦蹶項其治也約法以和民再
傳惠文則積漸太弛矣宣帝固挽之於精
嚴乎而法網寔峻急也唐太宗以英喆除
隋蹟難其治也惠浸於萌生迨至天寶則
醞釀兆釁矣宣宗固裁之於彊毅乎而督
責過刻覈也如宋則禪受肇基在太祖已
歎震疊之氣而忠厚貽脉至繼體俱多陵
替之形三德更何稱焉我
===
太祖高皇帝
統天神聖埽氈裘而盡畀之冠裳
成祖文皇帝應運明哲括華夷而總奠之符籙
猗與庥哉曁
列聖纘承道有升降政每因之固重熙累洽時
也而至于
今日爲尤盛遼陽獻馘雲谷來琛與咸賓重
punctuated: 此道矣。是道也，羹之鹽梅、酒之麴櫱，孰能廢之？偏重專一，政迺攸斁，緣此而張弛錯事也，洵其然與！三代而上，毋贅已。漢高祖以神武蹙秦蹶項，其治也，約法以和民；再傳惠、文，則積漸太弛矣。宣帝固挽之於精嚴乎，而法網寔峻急也。唐太宗以英喆除隋蹟難，其治也，惠浸於萌生；迨至天寶，則醞釀兆釁矣。宣宗固裁之於彊毅乎，而督責過刻覈也。如宋，則禪受肇基，在太祖已歎震疊之氣；而忠厚貽脉，至繼體俱多陵替之形，三德更何稱焉！我太祖高皇帝統天神聖，埽氈裘而盡畀之冠裳；成祖文皇帝應運明哲，括華夷而總奠之符籙。猗與庥哉！曁列聖纘承，道有升降，政每因之，固重熙累洽時也，而至于今日爲尤盛：遼陽獻馘，雲谷來琛，與咸賓重…
translation_en:
… this Way. As for this Way, it is like the salt and plum blossom used to season soup, or the yeast and malt used to brew wine—who could dispense with them? When one leans solely to one extreme, governance is thereby ruined; because of this, the alternation of tension and relaxation becomes disordered in practice. Is this not truly so? 

Of the Three Dynasties and earlier, there is no need to speak at length. Emperor Gaozu of Han (漢高祖), with divine martial prowess, pressed hard upon Qin and overthrew Xiang Yu (項羽); in his governance, he simplified the laws to bring harmony to the people. Yet after being passed down through Emperors Hui (惠帝) and Wen (文帝), it gradually became overly lax. Emperor Xuan (宣帝) certainly sought to pull it back through meticulous strictness, yet the net of the law became truly harsh and urgent. Emperor Taizong of Tang (唐太宗), with heroic wisdom, swept away the troubles left in the wake of Sui [? 除隋蹟難, for 靖難]; in his governance, his benevolence soaked into the multitude of the living. Yet by the Tianbao (天寶) era, troubles had been brewing and portents of strife appeared. Emperor Xuanzong (宣宗) certainly sought to restrain things with firm resolve, yet his supervision and censure were overly severe and exacting. As for Song, its foundation was laid through abdication, so that even under Emperor Taizu (太祖) there was already a lack [? 歎, for 歉] of awe-inspiring vigor; and though loyalty and generosity were bequeathed as the dynastic lifeblood, those who succeeded to the throne all showed many signs of decline and laxity—what more could be said of the Three Virtues (三德) there?

Our Grand Progenitor, Emperor Gao (太祖高皇帝), possessing heaven-ruling divine sageliness, swept away the felt-and-fur-clad barbarians and bestowed caps and robes upon all; the Accomplished Progenitor, Emperor Wen (成祖文皇帝), responding to destiny with brilliant wisdom, encompassed both Chinese and barbarian and settled them all under the imperial talismans and registers. Oh, how magnificent and auspicious! Coming down to the successive sage emperors who inherited the line, as the Way rose or declined, governance invariably adapted to it. It has truly been an era of cumulative splendor and enduring harmony, reaching its greatest flourishing in the present day: in Liaoyang (遼陽), the severed ears of slain enemies are presented, and from Yungu (雲谷), precious tribute arrives, sharing the same transformative influence as when all came as guests through repeated [interpreters]…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
譁者有同化矣百官脩輔庶政無闕與允
釐咸熙者有同治矣朝而聽政晡而視學
即古之昧爽日昃又曷以加焉
剛明嚴畏之沖聖迥不世出而忠藎一得者
尚餘杞慮此何以故也愚請以意見試諤
諤言之可乎夫
天子以一人垂拱
斧扆之上固神州赤縣所翹首頓顙嚮澤而共
主者也明則日月威則雷霆均喁切焉今
===
抗章廷諍者幾人矣及長孺之戇陸宣公
之直盡撫牘而日鑒否耶礪世子奪者幾
舉矣寵列笥章褫煩刑書者盡
臨軒而清問否耶世方豫泰而南越剝紀西靈
鼓釁其間潢池而嘯聚者往往告變人事
可思有若此天方降祥而孛彗生芒風霾
兆異其中苦旱荒而籲訴者在在有之天
變可畏又若此其無乃于剛柔寬猛之間
尚有調劑未適其宜者耶竊謂
punctuated: 譁者，有同化矣；百官脩輔，庶政無闕，與允釐咸熙者，有同治矣。朝而聽政，晡而視學，即古之昧爽日昃，又曷以加焉？剛明嚴畏之沖聖，迥不世出，而忠藎一得者，尚餘杞慮，此何以故也？愚請以意見，試諤諤言之，可乎？夫天子以一人垂拱斧扆之上，固神州赤縣所翹首頓顙、嚮澤而共主者也，明則日月，威則雷霆，均喁切焉。今抗章廷諍者幾人矣，及長孺之戇、陸宣公之直，盡撫牘而日鑒否耶？礪世子奪者幾舉矣，寵列笥章、褫煩刑書者，盡臨軒而清問否耶？世方豫泰，而南越剝紀，西靈鼓釁，其間潢池而嘯聚者，往往告變，人事可思有若此；天方降祥，而孛彗生芒，風霾兆異，其中苦旱荒而籲訴者，在在有之，天變可畏又若此。其無乃于剛柔寬猛之間，尚有調劑未適其宜者耶？竊謂
translation_en:
…translators [重譯, printed 重譁][?], share the same civilizing transformation; the hundred officials cultivate their assistance and the manifold affairs of government have no deficiencies, so that compared with the time when all offices were faithfully regulated and all achievements resplendent, it shares the same good order. Attending to government in the morning and visiting the imperial academy in the late afternoon—even the ancients who rose at dawn and toiled until the sun inclined to the west, how could they surpass this? Why is it, then, that when a youthful sage ruler of firm clarity and reverent awe so far surpasses ordinary ages, loyal subjects with a single humble insight still harbor the worries of Qi? May this foolish one beg to offer his own views and try to speak them with forthright candor?

Now the Son of Heaven, as the One Man letting his robes hang down with hands folded before the axe-embroidered screen, is assuredly the common lord toward whom the sacred land and red precincts raise their heads and bow their foreheads in longing for his beneficence; his brightness is like the sun and moon, his majesty like thunder and lightning, and all look up to him with eager yearning. Today, how many have submitted memorials to remonstrate at court? As for the bluntness of Changru [Ji An 汲黯] and the uprightness of Duke Xuan of Lu [Lu Zhi 陸贄], are their memorials all laid hand upon and examined daily, or not? How many acts of giving and taking away [予奪, printed 子奪] to sharpen the age have been carried out? Those favored with robes from the imperial coffers and insignia, and those stripped of rank and troubled with the books of punishment—are they all personally questioned by the Emperor advancing to the front platform, or not?

The age is just now enjoying ease and peace, yet in Southern Yue discipline is eroded [or rebellions stir], and in Xiling hostilities are drummed up, while in the midst of this those who band together and whistle to assemble in the palace ponds [as bandits] frequently report uprisings—human affairs give cause for reflection like this. Heaven is just now sending down auspicious signs, yet comets put forth rays, wind and dust-haze portend anomalies, and in the midst of this those suffering from drought and famine who cry out in appeal are to be found everywhere—heavenly portents are to be feared like this as well. Could it be that between firmness and gentleness, leniency and severity, there is still some blending and balancing that has not yet hit upon what is proper? I humbly submit that…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
主上君臨萬邦元元待命誠宜軫念疾苦湔滌
煩苛大霈休養之仁錫以和平之福而
乾斷之用必不可弛者尤宜審時度勢運量之
聖心而無緩圖可焉蓋
皇綱在御太阿在持洪庥景炎將自是而舄奕
之所以光紹
二祖而永無替于熙洽之治者意在斯矣草茅
愚生之見如此幸夫子之發愚覆也
第三問
馮時盛
===
同考試官訓導李〔時若〕批〔春秋論禮者多不究本原子能〕
考據精詳評議典正得立論之權衡矣
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批〔統論得失復重責備四子是有〕
筆法佳士佳士
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批〔開闔變化渠獲之森然〕
禮可爲國乎天經地義之緐敘也禮可觀
政乎大綱小紀之緐昭也蓋天下無一物
無禮君子不可斯須去禮天澤有定序緐
punctuated:
主上君臨萬邦，元元待命，誠宜軫念疾苦，湔滌煩苛，大霈休養之仁，錫以和平之福。而乾斷之用必不可弛者，尤宜審時度勢，運量之聖心而無緩圖可焉。蓋皇綱在御，太阿在持，洪庥景炎，將自是而舄奕，之所以光紹二祖，而永無替于熙洽之治者，意在斯矣。草茅愚生之見如此，幸夫子之發愚覆也。

第三問
馮時盛
同考試官訓導李〔時若〕批：〔《春秋》論禮者多不究本原，子能〕考據精詳，評議典正，得立論之權衡矣。
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批：〔統論得失，復重責備四子，是有〕筆法。佳士，佳士。
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批：〔開闔變化，渠獲之森然。〕

禮可爲國乎？天經地義之緐敘也。禮可觀政乎？大綱小紀之緐昭也。蓋天下無一物無禮，君子不可斯須去禮。天澤有定序，緐
translation_en:
… His Majesty rules over the myriad states, and the common people await his command. He should truly take pity on their sufferings, wash away burdensome and harsh measures, lavishly bestow the benevolence of rest and nourishment, and grant the blessings of peace and harmony. Yet as for the exercise of sovereign decisiveness, which must never be relaxed, it is especially fitting that he examine the times and weigh the circumstances, revolving and measuring them within his sacred mind without delay in planning. For when the imperial纲 [guiding ropes of rule] are in hand and the Tai'e sword of sovereign authority is firmly grasped, great blessings and resplendent glory will from this shine forth in unbroken succession; that by which he gloriously continues the work of the Two Ancestors (Taizu and Taizong) and never fails in maintaining a prosperous and harmonious rule surely lies in this. Such are the views of a rustic and foolish student; I hope only that the Master will lift the cover of my ignorance.

Question Three
Feng Shisheng 馮時盛
Comment by Associate Examiner Assistant Instructor Li Shiruo 李時若: Those in the Spring and Autumn period who discussed ritual mostly failed to investigate its fundamental source. You are able to examine the evidence with precision and detail, and your evaluations and discussions are canonical and correct; you have grasped the proper balance of constructing an argument.
Comment by Examiner Instructor Tian Younian 田有年: He comprehensively discusses merits and faults, and furthermore places heavy blame of perfection upon the four masters—this shows true historiographical style in writing. A fine scholar, a fine scholar!
Comment by Examiner Subprefectural Instructor Su Tinglong 蘇廷龍: With opening and closing and dynamic transitions, its rules and measures [reading 矩矱 for 渠獲] are strictly arrayed.

Can ritual be used to govern a state? It is the abundant ordering [?] of the invariable principle of Heaven and the rightful duty of Earth. Can ritual be used to observe governance? It is the abundant manifestation [?] of the great guiding principles and minor regulations. Indeed, there is not a single thing under Heaven without ritual, and the gentleman cannot depart from ritual even for an instant. Heaven and marsh have a fixed order; lavish…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
飾者淆之矣敦庸有常經惛嫚者拂之矣
知此則秉禮者不必司以總章而度可貞
觀禮者不必察之象物而論可定古之人
遠且湮矣千載而下令人撫卷咨嗟若親
與之上下論議而得失如在者何爲其然
哉嘗聞世之治也君子尚能而讓其下小
人農力以事其上是以上下有禮而讒慝
不興及其亂也君子稱其功以加小人小
人伐其技以馮君子是以上下無禮亂虐
===
竝至易之謙以制禮書之寅以和衷禮存
捭豚之節詩咏相鼠之章而麟經一書屬
詞比事所致重於禮教者意甚殷焉如加
牲載書以涖盟大蒐執秩以比賦聘頫有
雖貢藝程力凡征伐宴饗一有前茅簡璧
舉也紹介煌將登歌報獻而禮度胥無愆
隊也已故溯自二百四十餘禩以來邦幾
榮懷殄瘁矣人孰蕭艾蕙芷矣暨事之符
於道骫於法蹊徑多趨而判若鶩鼪者固
punctuated: 飾者淆之矣；敦庸有常經，惛嫚者拂之矣。知此，則秉禮者不必司以總章，而度可貞；觀禮者不必察之象物，而論可定。古之人遠且湮矣，千載而下，令人撫卷咨嗟，若親與之上下論議，而得失如在者，何爲其然哉？嘗聞世之治也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人農力以事其上，是以上下有禮，而讒慝不興；及其亂也，君子稱其功以加小人，小人伐其技以馮君子，是以上下無禮，亂虐竝至。《易》之「謙以制禮」，《書》之「寅以和衷」，《禮》存捭豚之節，《詩》咏《相鼠》之章，而《麟經》一書，屬詞比事，所致重於禮教者，意甚殷焉。如加牲載書以涖盟，大蒐執秩以比賦，聘頫有雖，貢藝程力，凡征伐、宴饗，一有前茅、簡璧舉也，紹介煌將，登歌報獻，而禮度胥無愆隊也已。故溯自二百四十餘禩以來，邦幾榮懷殄瘁矣，人孰蕭艾蕙芷矣，暨事之符於道、骫於法，蹊徑多趨，而判若鶩鼪者，固
translation_en:
…[those who indulge in excessive] ornamentation confuse it; honoring and employing the worthy have constant norms, yet the muddleheaded and arrogant violate them. Understanding this, those who uphold ritual propriety need not preside over the Grand Hall of Light (Zongzhang) for their standards to remain firm, and those who observe ritual propriety need not scrutinize symbolic emblems for their judgments to be settled. The people of antiquity are distant and long buried, yet a thousand years later they make one stroke the scroll and sigh, as though personally debating with them back and forth, with their successes and failures vividly present before us—why is this so?

I have heard that when the world is well governed, gentlemen esteem ability and yield to their subordinates, while petty men labor diligently to serve their superiors; thus superiors and inferiors observe ritual propriety, and slander and evil do not arise. When it falls into disorder, gentlemen boast of their achievements to lord it over petty men, while petty men vaunt their skills to encroach upon gentlemen; thus superiors and inferiors lack ritual propriety, and disorder and tyranny arrive together. The Book of Changes (Yi) speaks of "humility to institute rites"; the Book of Documents (Shu) speaks of "reverence to harmonize the inner moral sense"; the Book of Rites (Li) preserves the ancient usage of tearing apart roast suckling pig; the Book of Odes (Shi) sings the stanzas of "Look at the Rat" ("Xiangshu"); and the Unicorn Classic [Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)], in connecting words and arranging events, places an especially earnest emphasis on ritual teaching. For instance, placing the covenant text upon the sacrificial victim to preside over an alliance; holding a great hunting review and maintaining the order of ranks to assess military levies; conducting missions of inquiry and court visits with solemnity [?]; presenting tribute according to skill and measuring strength; and in all military expeditions and banquets, whenever advance scouts or ceremonies with jade tablets and disks were carried out, with intermediaries magnificently presenting offerings, and songs ascending from the hall in reciprocation and presentation—in all these, the ritual measures were without error or lapse. Therefore, tracing back over those more than two hundred and forty years, how many states flourished in tranquility or suffered exhaustion and distress, who among men were foul mugwort or fragrant orchids, and which affairs conformed to the Way or bent the law, pursuing divergent paths and differing like wild ducks and weasels [?]—indeed, none of these…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
不能終詭於禮焉以塗時人之耳目蓋禮
防民僞猶堤之障浠潦也涓勺逾之蟻之
朽壤得而隙之勢將盡隤其防而莫云閼
止大哉禮乎則以觀德德以處事事以度
功功以食民無可軼焉春秋亦叔世不古
若矣其所名禮仰質伯夷周公之所典制
孔子之所删定已爲土苴爲弁髦矧叔孫
通起於桴鼓間一何綿蕞猥鄙也而開元
慶曆聱牙訟聚竟何稱焉試卽春秋之議
===
禮者而析陳之管夷吾平戎於周饗以上
卿之禮曰臣賤有司也陪臣敢辭是讓也
貟不忘其君者也甯武子來聘於魯賦以
湛露之章曰臣爲肄業及也敢干大禮是
恭也誠其儀有淑者也宋之郜鼎寵賂行
也納於太廟章孰甚焉諫之以德臧孫達
其有後於魯乎莒之逋僕兇盜極也屬以
采邑誨孰甚焉驅之出境季文子其崇勸
於國乎伯石之汰也謂將及也一相禮而
punctuated: 不能終詭於禮焉，以塗時人之耳目。蓋禮防民僞，猶堤之障浠潦也。涓勺逾之，蟻之朽壤得而隙之，勢將盡隤其防而莫云閼止。大哉禮乎！則以觀德，德以處事，事以度功，功以食民，無可軼焉。春秋亦叔世，不古若矣。其所名禮，仰質伯夷、周公之所典制，孔子之所删定，已爲土苴、爲弁髦。矧叔孫通起於桴鼓間，一何綿蕞猥鄙也；而開元、慶曆，聱牙訟聚，竟何稱焉？試卽《春秋》之議禮者而析陳之：管夷吾平戎於周，饗以上卿之禮，曰：「臣，賤有司也，陪臣敢辭。」是讓也，貟不忘其君者也。甯武子來聘於魯，賦以《湛露》之章，曰：「臣爲肄業及也，敢干大禮？」是恭也，誠其儀有淑者也。宋之郜鼎，寵賂行也，納於太廟，章孰甚焉！諫之以德，臧孫達其有後於魯乎！莒之逋僕，兇盜極也，屬以采邑，誨孰甚焉！驅之出境，季文子其崇勸於國乎！伯石之汰也，謂將及也，一相禮而
translation_en: … cannot ultimately pervert ritual so as to blind the eyes and stop the ears of contemporaries. For ritual guards against the deceitfulness of the people just as a dike holds back floodwaters. If a trickle or a spoonful overflows it, or if ants find decayed earth and bore a gap through it, the momentum will inevitably collapse the entire barrier so that nothing can stem the flow. Great indeed is ritual! Rules serve to observe virtue, virtue to manage affairs, affairs to measure merit, and merit to nourish the people—none can go beyond this. The Spring and Autumn period was already an age of decline, not equal to antiquity. When what it called ritual is held up against the institutions established by Boyi 伯夷 and the Duke of Zhou 周公, or the texts edited and fixed by Confucius 孔子, it had already been treated as mere dregs of earth and cast-off caps. How much more so when Shusun Tong 叔孫通 rose amid drums and drumsticks—how vulgar and base was his rope-and-straw rehearsal! And in the Kaiyuan 開元 and Qingli 慶曆 eras, with their jarring disputes and gathered litigations, what was there worthy of praise after all? Let us examine and set forth in detail the discussions of ritual in the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu 春秋): When Guan Yiwu 管夷吾 pacified the Rong on behalf of Zhou and was feasted with the rites due a Senior Minister, he said: "Your servant is a lowly functionary; as a rear vassal, I dare decline." This wasyielding, and shows one who truly [?] did not forget his lord. When Ning Wuzi 甯武子 came on a mission of friendly inquiry to Lu and the stanza of "Heavy Dew" (Zhanlu 湛露) was recited for him, he said: "Your servant assumed it was merely mentioned as an exercise in study; how dare I encroach upon the great rites?" This was reverence, and truly showed one whose demeanor was virtuous. As for the cauldron of Gao from Song, it was the practice of favoring bribery; placing it in the Grand Ancestral Temple—what display of wrongdoing could be more glaring than that! By remonstrating on the basis of virtue, would Zang Sunda 臧孫達 not surely have descendants in Lu! As for the runaway servant from Ju, he was the ultimate in vicious banditry; bestowing a fief upon him—what inducement to crime could be worse than that! By driving him across the border, did Ji Wenzi 季文子 not exalt encouragement of the good in the state! As for Boshi 伯石, in his arrogance it was said disaster would overtake him, yet by once assisting in ritual and …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
獲晉君之賜禮其荷祿之基也已子產之
勳也謂上賞也一辭邑而多子展之績禮
其執政之繇也已勞賄無慾晉侯美昭公
矣女叔齊謂公室四分民食於他瑣屑習
儀無當也信知言與慶父兆難齊侯省閔
公矣仲孫湫謂親禮間攜務寧內難盟府
周禮尚存也良有見與繁纓名器寓焉朝
隧王度重焉于奚晉文之請舛也孔子惜
之天王飭之宜矣棠魚軌物章焉齊社朝
===
會行焉隱公莊公之觀侈也僖伯諫之曹
劌正之踸矣晏子謂禮與天地竝尚何田
氏之難已乎齊景自諉不能此君令臣共
之論徒令簡冊昭昭也遷啓疆謂聖王務
行禮尚何大夫之厚辱乎楚子亦已樂聞
然朝聘宴獻之規終其乾谿沒沒也春秋
之所謂禮大都概此然伐異黨同嘵嘵相
尚越禮自盭復援禮自文視先王之禮咸
無徵焉中有焜燿時尚而爲議禮家所稱
punctuated: 獲晉君之賜，禮其荷祿之基也已。子產之勳也，謂上賞也，一辭邑而多子展之績，禮其執政之繇也已。勞賄無慾，晉侯美昭公矣；女叔齊謂公室四分，民食於他，瑣屑習儀無當也，信知言與！慶父兆難，齊侯省閔公矣；仲孫湫謂親禮間攜，務寧內難，盟府周禮尚存也，良有見與！繁纓，名器寓焉；朝隧，王度重焉。于奚、晉文之請，舛也，孔子惜之，天王飭之，宜矣。棠魚，軌物章焉；齊社，朝會行焉。隱公、莊公之觀，侈也，僖伯諫之，曹劌正之，踸矣。晏子謂禮與天地竝，尚何田氏之難已乎？齊景自諉不能，此君令臣共之論，徒令簡冊昭昭也。遷啓疆謂聖王務行禮，尚何大夫之厚辱乎？楚子亦已樂聞，然朝聘宴獻之規，終其乾谿沒沒也。春秋之所謂禮，大都概此。然伐異黨同，嘵嘵相尚，越禮自盭，復援禮自文，視先王之禮，咸無徵焉。中有焜燿時尚，而爲議禮家所稱
translation_en:
…received the gifts of the ruler of Jin—ritual propriety was indeed the foundation for sustaining his emolument! In the case of Zichan's 子產 merit, it was deemed worthy of the highest reward, yet by declining the fiefs and praising the achievements of Zizhan 子展, ritual propriety was indeed the path by which he came to hold the reins of government!

Showing no lapse in the ceremonies of greeting and gift-giving, the Marquis of Jin praised Duke Zhao 昭公 [of Lu]; yet Ru Shuqi 女叔齊 said that with the ducal house divided into four and the people drawing their livelihood from others, practicing petty ceremonial deportment was beside the point—truly, did he not know how to judge words! When Qingfu 慶父 stirred up trouble, the Marquis of Qi sent to inquire after Duke Min 閔公 [of Lu]; Zhongsun Qiao 仲孫湫 advised staying close to those who uphold ritual propriety and sowing discord among the estranged, striving first to pacify internal troubles because the rituals of Zhou were still preserved in the archives of covenants—truly, did he not have keen insight!

In the ornamental馬-girth (fanying 繁纓), title and ritual vessel reside; in the royal tomb-tunnel (chaichui 朝隧) and audience, kingly regulations carry great weight. The requests of Zhongshu Yuxi 仲叔于奚 and Duke Wen of Jin 晉文公 were perverse; that Confucius regretted the one and the Heavenly King rebuked the other was fitting indeed. In the fishing at Tang 棠, the regular norms and emblems were made manifest; at the altar of the soil in Qi, court audiences and assemblies were conducted. The sightseeing of Duke Yin 隱公 and Duke Zhuang 莊公 was extravagant; that臧 Xibo 臧僖伯 remonstrated against the one and Cao Gui 曹劌 corrected the other was well-founded [?] indeed.

Yanzi 晏子 said that ritual propriety stands on a par with Heaven and Earth—how then could the usurpation of the Tian 田 clan not have been stopped? Yet Duke Jing of Qi 齊景公 excused himself as incapable, so that this discourse on the ruler commanding and the minister obeying merely left a shining record in the historical bamboo slips. Wei Qijiang 薳啓疆 [written 遷啓疆] said that the sage kings strove to practice ritual propriety—how then could the grandees be subjected to heavy humiliation? The Viscount of Chu was pleased to hear this, yet the admonition regarding court visits, missions, banquets, and presentations ended in his perishing in obscurity at Ganxi 乾谿.

What the Spring and Autumn period called ritual propriety was by and large like this. Yet in attacking those who differed and siding with those of their own faction, they clamorously tried to outdo one another; transgressing ritual propriety in their own perversity, they then cited ritual propriety to gloss over their actions. Compared with the rituals of the former kings, none of it could be substantiated. Among them, those who dazzled the fashion of their age and were praised and…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
引者管子諸人其最著也然亦豈無訾議
乎哉管子天下才也謂宜世祀乎內政懷
譎塞門樹僭而易牙開方之竝列何取焉
時方隘其器矣子產古遺愛也謂誠惠人
乎丘賦慢作謗政繁興而參辟刑書之禁
禦何爲焉時方病其政矣季文子社稷之
衞僑如亟稱然矣宣公簒立夷子敗紀是
可緘嘿雖後世不能無猜也晏子仁人之
言景公省刑得矣三士起尕萊人播歌是
===
孰貽戚卽嗣世不能無憾也蓋偉其事而
稱之則數子春秋之良也燁庥光垂後奕
秉德媚禮鄰國莫敢望焉若不宜索其眚
詬以重掩之如數其事而責焉則言詩書
動綱紀所蘧廬乎仁義而攘竊乎道德者
名與實十九不相讎是則所謂竅也均之
叛禮去矣噫嘻哉談禮者何易易也先王
制禮本寅直而略其繁縟後世用之拾糟
粕而棄其精華故雖曾以秉禮之國識者
punctuated: 引者，管子諸人其最著也。然亦豈無訾議乎哉？管子，天下才也，謂宜世祀乎？內政懷譎，塞門樹僭，而易牙、開方之竝列，何取焉？時方隘其器矣。子產，古遺愛也，謂誠惠人乎？丘賦慢作，謗政繁興，而參辟刑書之禁禦，何爲焉？時方病其政矣。季文子，社稷之衞，僑如亟稱，然矣；宣公簒立，夷子敗紀，是可緘嘿？雖後世不能無猜也。晏子，仁人之言，景公省刑，得矣；三士起尕，萊人播歌，是孰貽戚？卽嗣世不能無憾也。蓋偉其事而稱之，則數子春秋之良也，燁庥光垂後奕，秉德媚禮，鄰國莫敢望焉，若不宜索其眚詬以重掩之；如數其事而責焉，則言《詩》、《書》，動綱紀，所蘧廬乎仁義而攘竊乎道德者，名與實十九不相讎，是則所謂竅也，均之叛禮去矣。噫嘻哉！談禮者何易易也！先王制禮，本寅直而略其繁縟；後世用之，拾糟粕而棄其精華。故雖曾以秉禮之國，識者
translation_en: … cited, Guanzi 管子 and those several men are the most prominent. Yet how could they be free from criticism? Guanzi had a talent fit for the whole realm, so they said he deserved hereditary sacrifices—did he really? In domestic administration he harbored craftiness, with his screened gate he usurped prerogative, and as for placing Yiya 易牙 and Kaifang 開方 alongside him in court, what merit was there in that? His contemporaries already considered his vessel small! Zichan 子產 was the one of whom it was said, "His love is what was left behind from antiquity," so they said he was truly a benevolent man—was he really? The district military levies were arrogantly instituted, criticisms of his governance arose in profusion, and as for the prohibitions and defenses of his three-code Book of Punishments, what was the point of that? His contemporaries already found fault with his governance! Ji Wenzi 季文子 was the guardian of the altars of soil and grain, and Qiaoru 僑如 repeatedly praised him—that was true enough. Yet when Duke Xuan 宣公 usurped the throne and Yizi 夷子 ruined discipline, how could he remain silent? Even later generations cannot be without suspicion of him. Yanzi 晏子 spoke the words of a humane man, and Duke Jing 景公 reduced punishments—that was well done. Yet when the three warriors stirred up trouble [?] and the people of Lai 萊 spread songs of lament, who bequeathed such grief? Even succeeding generations cannot be without regret over him. Indeed, if we magnify their deeds and praise them, then these several men were the finest of the Spring and Autumn period: their radiant grace shone down to later ages, they upheld virtue and cleaved to ritual propriety so that neighboring states dared not hope to match them, and it would seem improper to search out their blemishes and disgraces so as to heavily obscure their merits. Yet if we tally their deeds and hold them strictly to account, then in speaking of the Odes (Shi 詩) and the Documents (Shu 書) and invoking the guiding principles of order, those who merely treated benevolence and righteousness as a temporary lodging and stole the name of morality failed nine times out of ten to make reputation match reality. This is what is meant by hollowness—all alike departed in rebellion from ritual propriety! Alas! How lightly do people speak of ritual propriety! When the former kings instituted the rites, they rooted them in reverence and uprightness while passing over elaborate minutiae; when later ages employed them, they picked up the dregs and cast away the essence. Thus, even with魯 [Lu, here printed 曾], a state that upheld ritual propriety, men of discernment…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
謂周禮盡在魯矣而吾猶見夫意如文姜
之事乞羅歸身之請而悲魯之與禮俱亡
也禮器曰先王之立禮也有本焉有文焉
無本不立無文不行今而後知用禮者之
汨陳其本也逢掖生非達禮者而顧學之
堇堇述其所睹記者若此惟執事折衷焉
第四問
李爲芝
同考試官訓導鍾〔國芝〕批〔備寫窮民艱苦之狀令人惻然且圖事揆策條分縷悉救荒得此流移知免溝壑矣〕
===
同考試官教諭高〔儀〕批〔士子談荒政類襲常語子獨能議剴切鑿鑿可行是嘗抱先憂者錄之〕
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批〔荒政縈陳末重守令確有識見〕
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批〔意懇詞直時事在目經術世務于子覘之矣敬羨敬羨〕
菑異盛世不免也未菑而先事綢繆之有
之不爲害方菑而多方勤恤之有之不爲
害蓋天心未嘗一日棄遺斯民惟數之適
punctuated:
謂「周禮盡在魯矣」，而吾猶見夫意如、文姜之事，乞羅、歸身之請，而悲魯之與禮俱亡也。《禮器》曰：「先王之立禮也，有本焉，有文焉；無本不立，無文不行。」今而後知用禮者之汨陳其本也。逢掖生非達禮者，而顧學之，堇堇述其所睹記者若此，惟執事折衷焉。

第四問
李爲芝
同考試官訓導鍾〔國芝〕批：〔備寫窮民艱苦之狀，令人惻然；且圖事揆策，條分縷悉。救荒得此，流移知免溝壑矣。〕
同考試官教諭高〔儀〕批：〔士子談荒政，類襲常語；子獨能議剴切，鑿鑿可行，是嘗抱先憂者。錄之。〕
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批：〔荒政縈陳，末重守令，確有識見。〕
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批：〔意懇詞直，時事在目；經術世務，于子覘之矣。敬羨，敬羨。〕

菑異，盛世不免也。未菑而先事綢繆之，有之不爲害；方菑而多方勤恤之，有之不爲害。蓋天心未嘗一日棄遺斯民，惟數之適
translation_en:
… said that "the rites of Zhou are all in Lu." Yet I still observe the affairs of Yiru (Jisun Yiru) and Wen Jiang, and the requests to beg for grain [reading 糴 for 羅] and to return in person [?], and I grieve that Lu perished together with its rites. The "Vessels of Rites" (Liqi) states: "In the former kings' establishment of rites, there was a root and there was pattern; without the root they cannot stand, and without pattern they cannot be put into practice." From this moment on, one knows that those who employ the rites have thrown their root into disorder. This scholar in wide-sleeved robes is not one who has mastered the rites, yet in striving to study them, I have merely recounted what I have seen and remembered like this; may Your Excellency judge and weigh it.

Fourth Question
Li Weizhi
Comment by Associate Examiner and Assistant Instructor Zhong Guozhi: "He fully depicts the hardships of the impoverished people, moving one to pity; moreover, in planning affairs and devising policies, he analyzes them item by item in thorough detail. With this for famine relief, vagrants and refugees will surely be spared from dying in ditches."
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Gao Yi: "When scholars discuss famine relief administration, they generally repeat commonplace phrases; you alone are able to argue with incisiveness, offering concrete and practicable measures—truly one who has long harbored far-sighted concern before trouble arises. Selected for inclusion."
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Tian Younian: "Famine relief policies are comprehensively set forth, and at the end emphasis is placed on prefects and magistrates; this truly shows insight."
Comment by Examiner and Subprefectural Instructor Su Tinglong: "The intent is earnest and the words forthright, bringing current affairs right before the eyes; both classical learning and practical statecraft can be glimpsed in you. Deeply admirable, deeply admirable."

Calamities and anomalies cannot be avoided even in a flourishing age. If before a calamity occurs one makes preparations in advance, then even if it happens it will do no harm; if while a calamity is occurring one diligently relieves it through multiple means, then even if it happens it will do no harm. For the mind of Heaven has never for a single day abandoned these people; it is only that the coincidences of fate …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
然者所可惕民瘼未甞不一日待命於上
而政之必然者所當圖惕則乖沴可彌圖
則捐瘠可甦此古之涖政遇菑者切於瘝
身急於捄焚而歲不爲厲也夫甞聞之天
菑流行何代無之堯湯撫運且然矣淳㳸
之化綦隆難歧備之豫也汎舟之役秦爾
輸粟以濟晉饑今秦猶古也固大有可慨
者焉蓋秦封俗尚亢厲用多呰窳地產半
确磽而桑稌者鮮一遇淋溢湯爲巨浸熯
===
魃爲虐遂至無禾乃今則歲大侵矣而延
平慶陽間爲烈焉所在田隴甌窶者已枯
矣汙邪者如燬矣比屋丘墟頹垣壞壁僮
爲坏土矣逃移蔽野而下破釜敝帚老稚
相將決踵曳裾形容枯立十步九蹟倀倀
莫知所之固輾轉爲溝中之瘠矣傷瘨之
狀見者茹酸愁吝之聲聞者飲泣賈誼不
能盡其痛鄭俠不能繪其似斯民也何以
生哉蓋歉歲多逋賦而荒政首蠲征況軍
punctuated: 然者所可惕；民瘼未甞不一日待命於上，而政之必然者所當圖。惕則乖沴可彌，圖則捐瘠可甦。此古之涖政遇菑者，切於瘝身，急於捄焚，而歲不爲厲也。夫甞聞之：「天菑流行，何代無之？」堯、湯撫運，且然矣，淳㳸之化綦隆，難歧備之豫也。「汎舟之役」，秦爾輸粟以濟晉饑。今秦猶古也，固大有可慨者焉。蓋秦封俗尚亢厲，用多呰窳，地產半确磽，而桑稌者鮮。一遇淋溢，湯爲巨浸；熯魃爲虐，遂至無禾。乃今則歲大侵矣，而延、平、慶陽間爲烈焉。所在田隴，甌窶者已枯矣，汙邪者如燬矣；比屋丘墟，頹垣壞壁，僮爲坏土矣。逃移蔽野而下，破釜敝帚，老稚相將，決踵曳裾，形容枯立，十步九蹟，倀倀莫知所之，固輾轉爲溝中之瘠矣。傷瘨之狀，見者茹酸；愁吝之聲，聞者飲泣。賈誼不能盡其痛，鄭俠不能繪其似。斯民也，何以生哉？蓋歉歲多逋賦，而荒政首蠲征，況軍
translation_en:
…is what should inspire vigilance; the sufferings of the people never cease for a single day to await relief from above, and the necessary measures of governance are what must be planned. With vigilance, disharmonious and noxious influences can be quelled; with planning, the starving and emaciated can be revived. For this reason, those who administered government in antiquity and encountered disasters felt them as acutely as pain in their own bodies, acted as urgently as if rescuing people from fire, and thus the year's dearth did not become a plague.

Indeed, I have heard it said: "Natural disasters occur in turn; what era is free of them?" Even when Yao and Tang held the mandate, it was so; yet because their pure and generous transformative influence was supremely abundant, it was hard to fault [?] their advance preparedness. In the "Boat-Floating Campaign," Qin even transported grain to relieve the famine in Jin. The Qin of today is the same land as in antiquity, yet there is truly much to lament! For across the territory of Qin, customs incline toward fierce harshness, livelihoods are often shiftless and crude, half the land is stony and barren, and those who cultivate mulberry and glutinous rice are few. Whenever torrential rains strike, the land surges into a vast flood; when the drought-demon wreaks havoc, not a single stalk of grain is left.

Now the year has suffered a great famine, which is especially severe across Yan'an, Pingliang, and Qingyang. Everywhere among the fields and dikes, the high mounds have already withered, and the low-lying marshes look as though scorched by fire. Row upon row of houses lie in ruins; with crumbling walls and broken partitions, they are reduced to mere mounds of earth [?]. Refugees cover the wilderness as they stream down, carrying cracked cauldrons and worn-out brooms, old and young supporting one another, their heels split and garments dragging, their figures withered as they stand, stumbling nine times in every ten steps, wandering aimlessly without knowing where to go—surely destined to toss and turn until they become emaciated corpses in the ditches. At the sight of their grievous affliction, onlookers swallow bitter sorrow; at the sound of their mournful cries, listeners weep silently. Jia Yi 賈誼 could not fully express their anguish, nor could Zheng Xia 鄭俠 paint their likeness. These people—how are they to survive?

In years of dearth there are many tax arrears, and famine administration places the remission of levies first. How much more so when military…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
旅頻年徵發西北民力殫矣今郎敲扑煩
焉檄令亟焉亦何所析斃以充儋石不若
徼恩
主上覃寬恤之條下盡蠲之令以蘇此元元雖
軍有額共難以皐緩而夙所積貯如蘭肅
等處獨不可蒐括抵解一歲以緩路殣旦
夕之命乎秦中郡縣固
國家肢體也一肢莫舉則餘者難以獨運窮
邑將至無民而肢膝殆浸淫入於廢矣郡
===
縣長吏尚可析之而秦越異視耶私家厚
藏徙有於無公廪歲積衰多於寡則涸鮒
庶幾有斗水之望乎如曰已且未傴而轉
輸者盡閑之糴歲均苦侵而流寓者悉禦
諸境則子遺立呫之危矣爲人上者方蹙
頞悔心而何此忍也不聞大侵之禮詳在
穀梁者乎君食不兼味也臺榭不塗也弛
候迎道不除百官修而不制鬼神禱而不
祀修省昭度制委悉矣而非竊示彌文焉
punctuated: 旅頻年徵發，西北民力殫矣。今郎敲扑煩焉，檄令亟焉，亦何所析斃以充儋石？不若徼恩主上，覃寬恤之條，下盡蠲之令，以蘇此元元。雖軍有額共，難以皐緩，而夙所積貯，如蘭、肅等處，獨不可蒐括抵解一歲，以緩路殣旦夕之命乎？秦中郡縣，固國家肢體也。一肢莫舉，則餘者難以獨運；窮邑將至無民，而肢膝殆浸淫入於廢矣。郡縣長吏，尚可析之而秦越異視耶？私家厚藏，徙有於無；公廪歲積，衰多於寡，則涸鮒庶幾有斗水之望乎！如曰已且未傴，而轉輸者盡閑之糴；歲均苦侵，而流寓者悉禦諸境，則子遺立呫之危矣。爲人上者方蹙頞悔心，而何此忍也？不聞大侵之禮詳在《穀梁》者乎？君食不兼味也，臺榭不塗也，弛候迎，道不除，百官修而不制，鬼神禱而不祀。修省昭度，制委悉矣，而非竊示彌文焉…
translation_en: …[military] expeditions have been levied year after year, the strength of the people in the northwest is exhausted. Even if one now applies the rod repeatedly and issues urgent writs and orders, how could anything be wrung from these dying people [?] to fill even a jar or a picul of grain? It would be better to implore grace from the Sovereign above, extending articles of leniency and compassion and issuing an order for a complete tax remission so as to revive the common people. Although the military has fixed quotas of supplies that are difficult to delay at length, as for the grain long stored up in places such as Lanzhou and Suzhou, could we not alone gather and draw upon it to offset a year's deliveries, thereby prolonging from morning to evening the lives of those starving by the roadside? The commanderies and counties within Shaanxi are indeed the limbs and body of the State. When one limb cannot be raised, it is hard for the rest to function alone; when destitute districts are on the verge of having no people left, the limbs and knees are gradually sinking into paralysis. How can the chief officials of the commanderies and counties still divide themselves from one another and look upon each other's plight with the indifference of Qin and Yue? If the ample stores of private families are shifted from where there is plenty to where there is nothing, and the annual reserves of the public granaries are taken from the abundant to augment the scarce, then the stranded fish in a dry rut may perhaps have hope of a peck of water! If instead they say that they themselves are not yet provided for [?] and completely bar those transporting grain from purchasing it, or say that the year is equally afflicted by dearth everywhere and drive away all refugees at the borders, then the surviving remnant will immediately stand on the brink of peril. When those who govern above are knitting their brows in remorse, how could they bear to do such a thing? Have you not heard of the rites for a great famine set forth in detail in the Guliang Commentary (Guliang zhuan)? The ruler's meals do not include double savories; terraces and pavilions are not plastered; watchmen and welcoming escorts [?] are relaxed; roads are not swept clean; the hundred officials keep their offices in order but make no new regulations; and prayers are offered to the spirits and gods without sacrificial offerings. In cultivating self-reflection and manifesting restraint, these regulations are thorough indeed, and are not merely an outward display of empty formality…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
已也不聞荒政之聚備存周禮者乎散省
利也薄征榷也緩刑弛力舍禁去幾索鬼
神除盜賊省禮殺哀蕃樂多婚興祛覃惠
政周密矣而非緣飾繁節焉已也汲長孺
發倉賑貧矯詔不問得濟事之權韓昌黎
請罷稅糧逋負勿逮達恤民之體兩浙告
饑增米價以通商趙清獻之見踔矣余杭
歲儲弛鹽禁以便民張忠定之識偉矣范
文正宴遊興造疏者乃斥其非是乎而其
===
惠則甚偏焉朱元晦依格請授斬者乃首
示不信乎而其意則良殷焉蓋天心仁愛
未忍遽絕斯民而諸臣者亦復傷民生之
不辰慮國本之先撥左提右挈朝摹夕畫
所大起屯蹇爲閭閻請命者斤斤不遺餘
策卒也丕濟時艱斡旋氣運此其炳若較
著者而移民移粟設糜給粥不與焉無迺
呂祖謙謂之下策姑置之歟嗚乎此亦未
可易言之也誠一舉之無慮蟻集無厭瑣
punctuated: 已也。不聞荒政之聚，備存《周禮》者乎？散省利也，薄征榷也，緩刑弛力，舍禁去幾，索鬼神，除盜賊，省禮殺哀，蕃樂多婚；興祛覃惠，政周密矣，而非緣飾繁節焉已也。汲長孺發倉賑貧，矯詔不問，得濟事之權；韓昌黎請罷稅糧，逋負勿逮，達恤民之體。兩浙告饑，增米價以通商，趙清獻之見踔矣；余杭歲儲，弛鹽禁以便民，張忠定之識偉矣。范文正宴遊興造，疏者乃斥其非是乎，而其惠則甚偏焉；朱元晦依格請授，斬者乃首示不信乎，而其意則良殷焉。蓋天心仁愛，未忍遽絕斯民，而諸臣者亦復傷民生之不辰，慮國本之先撥，左提右挈，朝摹夕畫，所大起屯蹇、爲閭閻請命者，斤斤不遺餘策。卒也丕濟時艱，斡旋氣運，此其炳若較著者，而移民移粟、設糜給粥不與焉。無迺呂祖謙謂之下策，姑置之歟？嗚乎！此亦未可易言之也。誠一舉之，無慮蟻集，無厭瑣…
translation_en: …only. Have you not heard how the gatherings of famine-relief administration are fully preserved in the Rites of Zhou (Zhouli)? Distributing relief and economizing on profit; reducing taxes and imposts; mitigating punishments and relaxing labor services; lifting prohibitions and abolishing customs inspections; seeking out ghosts and spirits and eliminating bandits and thieves; simplifying rituals and moderating mourning; setting aside music and multiplying marriages—in promoting aid, dispelling distress, and extending bounty, the administration is comprehensive and thorough, and is not merely a matter of adorning it with elaborate formalities. Ji Changru [Ji An] opened the granaries to relieve the poor, and his forging of an imperial decree went unpunished, for he grasped the expediency needed to accomplish the task; Han Changli [Han Yu] requested the remission of grain taxes and that those in arrears not be arrested, attaining the proper substance of compassion for the people. When the Two Zhe regions reported famine, raising rice prices to attract merchants showed how transcendent was the insight of Zhao Qingxian [Zhao Bian]; when Yuhang suffered a lean year [? 歲儲], relaxing the salt monopoly to convenience the people showed how magnificent was the discernment of Zhang Zhongding [Zhang Yong]. Fan Wenzheng [Fan仲淹, Fan Zhongyan] engaged in feasting, excursions, and construction works—those who submitted memorials denounced him as wrong, yet his beneficence was most widespread [? 偏 for 遍]; Zhu Yuanhui [Zhu Xi] requested official appointments for donors according to the regulations—those who withheld approval were the first to display distrust, yet his intentions were truly earnest. Indeed, the heart of Heaven is benevolent and loving, not bearing to suddenly cut off these people; and those ministers likewise grieved that the people's livelihood fell upon untimely days and worried lest the foundation of the state be first uprooted. Supporting one another on left and right, planning from morning till night, in greatly lifting the people from difficulty and distress and pleading for the lives of the common folk in the villages, they were assiduous and spared no strategy. In the end, they grandly relieved the difficulties of the times and turned around the destiny of the age. These are examples that are bright and clearly manifest, and yet moving populations, transferring grain, setting up gruel kitchens, and distributing congee are not even counted among them. Could it not be that because Lü Zuqian called these the "lowest policy," they have been set aside for the moment? Alas! This too cannot be spoken of lightly. If one truly carries them out, without worrying about people gathering like ants and without begrudging the petty…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
委卽一須臾之間可以起枯振槁而數萬
之命方引而長抑下第云乎今尚嬉虞之
矣約而論之其責在守令夫守令日親民
啚非徒假位號以奔走寰寓者凡斯民之
悴苦湮鬱顚連噢咻皆稔習而備諳之故
昕夕所有事催爾畊焉促爾織焉責爾賦
輸豐爾於槖之委積寬爾如毛之法令焉
呴沫然家人父子情相屬也卽一旦不虞
饑饉夭札之會逄豆區釜鍾之輿發饘於
===
是粥於是無不人人得而未見委溝壑胥
草野者則以良長吏體恤傾至而所憑藉
者厚也是故王制三年九年之蓄言備之
貴豫耳荀卿本末源流之論言捄之貴時
耳微良守令吾誰與歸乎不然刻覈沽聞
視民之痛癢若不相關爲獺爲鸇復驅而
竄去之迺有路殍遺骼枕藉相望萑苻不
逞揭竿而起者勢如矣有牧愛之責者如
之何自以其赤子擠之危而陷之盜也捄
punctuated: 委，卽一須臾之間可以起枯振槁，而數萬之命方引而長，抑下第云乎？今尚嬉虞之矣。約而論之，其責在守令。夫守令日親民啚，非徒假位號以奔走寰寓者，凡斯民之悴苦湮鬱、顚連噢咻，皆稔習而備諳之。故昕夕所有事，催爾畊焉，促爾織焉，責爾賦輸，豐爾於槖之委積，寬爾如毛之法令焉，呴沫然家人父子情相屬也。卽一旦不虞饑饉夭札之會，逄豆區釜鍾之輿發，饘於是，粥於是，無不人人得，而未見委溝壑、胥草野者，則以良長吏體恤傾至，而所憑藉者厚也。是故《王制》三年九年之蓄，言備之貴豫耳；荀卿本末源流之論，言捄之貴時耳。微良守令，吾誰與歸乎？不然，刻覈沽聞，視民之痛癢若不相關，爲獺爲鸇，復驅而竄去之，迺有路殍遺骼、枕藉相望，萑苻不逞、揭竿而起者，勢如矣。有牧愛之責者，如之何自以其赤子擠之危而陷之盜也？捄
translation_en:
… details, then within a single moment one can revive the withered and rouse the parched, and tens of thousands of lives will be prolonged. How can this merely be called an inferior measure? Yet nowadays people still treat it with complacent unconcern.

To sum it up, the responsibility lies with the prefects and magistrates. Prefects and magistrates are daily close to the people and the rural districts; they are not merely those who borrow official rank and title to bustle about the empire. Everything about these people—their haggard distress and pent-up gloom, their helplessness and cries of pain—they are thoroughly familiar with and completely understand. Therefore, in all their affairs from morning to night, they urge on your plowing, press on your weaving, exact your tax deliveries, enrich the stores accumulated in your sacks, and relax laws and ordinances that are as numerous as hairs, moistening one another with spittle in mutual care, bound together in affection like family members, fathers, and sons. Thus, even if one day there is an unexpected juncture of famine and pestilence, when grain is transported and distributed by the dou, ou, fu, and zhong measures, thick gruel is made here and thin congee is made there; there is no one who does not receive his share, and none are seen cast into ditches or perishing together in the wilds. This is because good senior local officials show wholehearted sympathy and care, and the resources relied upon are substantial. Therefore, the three-year and nine-year reserves in the Royal Regulations (Wangzhi) simply mean that in preparation, the essential thing is foresight; Xunzi's (Xun Qing 荀卿) discourse on root and branch, source and stream, simply means that in relief, the essential thing is timeliness. Without good prefects and magistrates, to whom could I turn?

Otherwise, if officials are harsh and calculating in order tofish for a reputation, viewing the pains and afflictions of the people as if they were of no concern, acting like otters and hawks that drive fish and birds into hiding, then corpses of the starved and unburied bones will lie heaped in view of one another along the roads, and desperadoes in the reed marshes will raise poles in rebellion—such will inevitably be the trend! How can those who bear the responsibility of shepherding and loving the people themselves push their own infants into peril and drive them into banditry? Does famine…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
荒果無善政哉得一賢長吏則福星滿路
歲不爲饑故遴長吏者當致謹也然愚願
有進焉省歲者在
朝廷敬天勤民務舉其重且鉅者省月日者
卿士庶職也展采錯事亦未可後巳斯則
爲綢繆爲勤恤有堯湯之備而反沴爲和
所大造三秦者其在今日乎夫民爲邦本
愚也目睹其殫殘流離之狀政有慝焉郎
執事不以問固將請之
===
第五問
郭僑
同考試官教諭祝〔推敬〕批〔夷狄款貢〕
國家大利也顧今邊事稍玩矣通篇條析利害兼陳振飭之策亦諳邊務者錄之
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批〔備詐虜情籌畫曲當取之不徒〕
以其文之麗也
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批〔書生譚邊計而利害曲折言言〕
中竅不凡材也
中國統禦夷狄毋好戰慎勿忘戰毋黷兵
punctuated:
荒果無善政哉？得一賢長吏，則福星滿路，歲不爲饑。故遴長吏者，當致謹也。然愚願有進焉：省歲者在朝廷，敬天勤民，務舉其重且鉅者；省月日者，卿士庶職也，展采錯事，亦未可後巳。斯則爲綢繆、爲勤恤，有堯湯之備，而反沴爲和，所大造三秦者，其在今日乎！夫民爲邦本，愚也目睹其殫殘流離之狀，政有慝焉，郎執事不以問，固將請之。

第五問
郭僑
同考試官教諭祝〔推敬〕批〔夷狄款貢，〕國家大利也。顧今邊事稍玩矣，通篇條析利害，兼陳振飭之策，亦諳邊務者，錄之。
考試官教諭田〔有年〕批〔備詐虜情，籌畫曲當，取之不徒〕以其文之麗也。
考試官學正蘇〔廷龍〕批〔書生譚邊計，而利害曲折，言言〕中竅，不凡材也。
中國統禦夷狄，毋好戰，慎勿忘戰；毋黷兵，
translation_en:
… relief truly lack good governance? If one obtains a single worthy senior local official, then a star of good fortune fills the roads, and the year does not become a famine. Therefore, those who select senior local officials must exercise the utmost care. Yet I, in my simplicity, wish to offer something further: examining the year as a whole rests with the Court, which by revering Heaven and laboring for the people must attend to what is weighty and great; examining the months and days rests with the high ministers, noblemen, and the various officials, who in displaying their capabilities and carrying out affairs must likewise not lag behind. In this way there will be both advance preparation and diligent compassion; possessing the readiness of Yao and Tang, and turning pernicious airs back into harmony, that which brings great blessing to the Three Qin [Shaanxi]—does it not lie in the present day! Now, the people are the foundation of the state. Having witnessed with my own eyes their exhaustion, ruin, and displacement, I feel deep distress [? 政有慝焉, reading 政 as Hr/心痛 or "there are defects in governance"]; even if Your Honor had not asked about it [reading 郎 as 即], I would surely have begged to speak of it.

Fifth Question
Guo Qiao 郭僑
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhu Tuijing 祝推敬, comments: When the barbarians submit and present tribute, it is a great benefit to the state. Yet at present, frontier affairs have grown somewhat lax. The entire essay analyzes the advantages and disadvantages point by point, and also sets forth policies for rousing and putting our defenses in order. He is indeed someone well-versed in frontier affairs; we record it for publication.
Examiner, Instructor Tian Younian 田有年, comments: He thoroughly details [? 備詳/備詐] the conditions of the northern caitiffs, and his strategic planning is nuanced and fitting. We select him not merely for the elegance of his prose.
Examiner, Director of Studies Su Tinglong 蘇廷龍, comments: A scholar-student discusses frontier strategy, yet in all the intricacies of advantage and disadvantage, every word hits the mark. He is a talent out of the ordinary.

In governing and controlling the barbarians, China must not be fond of war, yet must carefully guard against forgetting war; it must not wantonly employ troops, …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
憤勿弛兵戰數疲民連兵耗國不戰將自
焚如之何可好且黷也然一有不飭則狡
焉以啓封疆患者蠢蠢然矣奚所恃以來
不庭今之邊備無迺偷玩而狃於忘且弛
耶徹桑徙薪以大詰戎兵誠今日所當亹
亹講圖者也在秦言秦籌邊急焉聊稱引
往緒以及時事可乎夷狄跳患粤古有之
其散陳於詩書之所睹記格三苗克鬼方
于襄玁狁攘夷駿烈垂麻光爲奕神明者
===
迄今震之其它無論已至漢孝武靈威顯
鑠舉毛幕窮醜一時遣四大將軍出上谷
雁門代隴間蹀血萬里空無王庭雖財饟
士馬不無捐耗延再數傳積威所慴稽顙
接踵未敢一矢相加遺撫卷繫思一何偉
也與其忘且弛焉漢武可盡非耶我
祖宗汎掃胡元電走雷驅
鴻功茂烈超軼無前固將貽萬世治安而區區
醜虜無足貽慮矣迨今迺有不然者陝以
punctuated:
憤勿弛兵。戰數疲民，連兵耗國，不戰將自焚，如之何可好且黷也？然一有不飭，則狡焉以啓封疆患者，蠢蠢然矣，奚所恃以來不庭？今之邊備，無迺偷玩而狃於忘且弛耶？徹桑徙薪，以大詰戎兵，誠今日所當亹亹講圖者也。在秦言秦，籌邊急焉，聊稱引往緒以及時事可乎？

夷狄跳患，粤古有之。其散陳於《詩》、《書》之所睹記：格三苗、克鬼方、于襄玁狁，攘夷駿烈，垂麻光、爲奕神明者，迄今震之，其它無論已。至漢孝武靈威顯鑠，舉毛幕窮醜，一時遣四大將軍出上谷、雁門、代、隴間，蹀血萬里，空無王庭。雖財饟士馬不無捐耗，延再數傳，積威所慴，稽顙接踵，未敢一矢相加遺。撫卷繫思，一何偉也！與其忘且弛焉，漢武可盡非耶？

我祖宗汎掃胡元，電走雷驅，鴻功茂烈，超軼無前，固將貽萬世治安，而區區醜虜無足貽慮矣。迨今迺有不然者。陝以
translation_en:
… [take care] not to slacken the military. Frequent warfare exhausts the people, and continuous campaigning depletes the state; without fighting, one will burn oneself—how then can one be fond of war and wantonly resort to arms? Yet the moment there is any lack of readiness, those cunningly waiting to stir up trouble on the frontiers will begin wriggling into motion; what then could we rely upon to make the unsubmissive come to court? Are our present frontier defenses not perhaps lax and neglectful, accustomed to forgetting war and slackening the military? Gathering mulberry bark before it rains and moving firewood away from the chimney, so as to grandly attend to military weaponry—this is truly what ought to be tirelessly discussed and planned today. Speaking of Qin from within Qin [Shaanxi], planning for the frontier is urgent; may I tentatively cite threads from the past and extend them to current affairs?

The rampant menace of the barbarians has existed since antiquity. As for what is scattered throughout the records seen in the Classic of Poetry (Shi) and the Classic of History (Shu)—bringing the Three Miao to submission, conquering the Guifang, and driving out the Xianyun—these grand exploits of repelling the barbarians have handed down beneficent glory [麻 for 休] and shone upon their divine descendants [?], so that even down to the present day people are awed by them; of other matters there is no need to speak. Coming to Emperor Xiaowu of the Han [Emperor Wu], his numinous majesty shone brilliantly. To sweep away the vile hordes of the felt tents and desert [毛幕 for 氈幕], he simultaneously dispatched four Generals-in-Chief to march out between Shanggu, Yanmen, Dai, and Long, treading in blood for ten thousand li until the desert was emptied of any royal court of the Xiongnu. Although wealth, provisions, soldiers, and horses were not without loss and exhaustion, extending over several more generations, cowed by his accumulated majesty, they knocked their heads on the ground in continuous succession and never dared to shoot a single arrow at us. Laying a hand on the scroll and reflecting upon it, how magnificent it was! Compared to forgetting war and slackening the military, can Emperor Wu of the Han be entirely faulted?

Our Imperial Ancestors swept away the barbarian Yuan, driving them off like lightning and thunder. Their vast achievements and flourishing exploits surpassed everything before them; truly they were about to bequeath peace and order for ten thousand generations, and the petty, vile caitiffs were not worth leaving any worry behind. Coming down to the present, however, there are things that are not so. West of Shaan…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
西朔方諸內地自火篩竊渡內訌吉囊俺
蹶日甚入我郭邪迭我郊坰蹂躪我圍牧
屠僇我黔黎絕我保聚夷庚擄掠兇慘銜
恨者思滅此而後朝食矣頃俺酋以伊孫
內質故屢上書乞守外藩時河西虜奔遁
彌伏如雲谷約十年生聚十年訓練封疆
不聳穡人成功晉大夫之言明有徵哉一
時有事諸臣瀝肝攄藎不遺餘力而劃隆
帶礪澤流寰寓生靈者載在盟府邇來卒
===
伍忘戰日久不復計虜呼糧則衷甲攘功
則裂眦匿榜於通逵矯矢於官邸此其小
者也焚逼寺廨戕賊主將瀆已弁髦盡矣
往者雲中白下變故譚之令人扼腕今可
再熾耶誠所謂軍驕遺患者黠虜胆茹嘉
隆間黃甫川之殘破安定塞之深入瓦楂
梁全軍覆沒跳跋情形曷可更僕盡雖縻
以款貢羽檄少清然靖虜峽口之劫制頻
仍洮岷中大掠番族酒泉絕域今擁腫剝
punctuated: 西朔方諸內地，自火篩竊渡內訌，吉囊、俺蹶日甚，入我郭邪，迭我郊坰，蹂躪我圍牧，屠僇我黔黎，絕我保聚、夷庚。擄掠兇慘，銜恨者思滅此而後朝食矣。頃俺酋以伊孫內質故，屢上書乞守外藩。時河西虜奔遁，彌伏如雲谷約。十年生聚，十年訓練，封疆不聳，穡人成功，晉大夫之言明有徵哉！一時有事諸臣，瀝肝攄藎，不遺餘力，而劃隆帶礪、澤流寰寓生靈者，載在盟府。邇來卒伍忘戰日久，不復計虜，呼糧則衷甲，攘功則裂眦，匿榜於通逵，矯矢於官邸，此其小者也；焚逼寺廨，戕賊主將，瀆已弁髦盡矣。往者雲中、白下變故，譚之令人扼腕，今可再熾耶？誠所謂「軍驕遺患」者。黠虜胆茹，嘉、隆間黃甫川之殘破、安定塞之深入、瓦楂梁全軍覆沒，跳跋情形，曷可更僕盡！雖縻以款貢，羽檄少清，然靖虜峽口之劫制頻仍，洮、岷中大掠番族，酒泉絕域今擁腫剝…
