translation_en:
…west of Shaanxi, the interior territories of Shuofang and neighboring regions—ever since Huoshai stealthily crossed the river to stir up internal strife, and Jinang and Altan [read 俺答 for 俺蹶] grew daily more rampant—have seen them enter our outer walls, repeatedly invade our outskirts and frontier pastures, trample our enclosures and grazing lands, slaughter our common people, and cut off our fortified settlements and main thoroughfares. Their plundering and pillaging were so fierce and慘 cruel that those harboring resentment wished to destroy them before eating breakfast. Recently, because his grandson came in as a hostage, the chieftain Altan repeatedly submitted letters begging to guard the outer藩 frontier as a vassal. At that time, the caitiffs west of the Yellow River fled and hid themselves away, submitting completely to the Yunzhong-Shangu [?] pact. Ten years of gathering and multiplying, ten years of training and drilling; the frontiers are not alarmed, and the farmers achieve success—how clearly verified are the words of the grandee of Jin! The various officials involved in the affair at the time poured out their hearts and displayed their loyalty, sparing no effort; those who carved out lofty honors bound by the oath of river and whetstone, causing blessings to flow to living souls throughout the realm, have their merits recorded in the Archive of Covenants.

Lately, however, the troops in the ranks have forgotten warfare for a long time and no longer give thought to the caitiffs. When clamoring for rations they wear armor under their clothes; when seizing credit for merit they glare with splitting eye-corners. Posting anonymous placards on main thoroughfares and shooting arrows at official residences—these are merely the minor offenses; burning and threatening government offices and murdering their commanding generals show that insubordination has cast aside all restraint like a discarded cap. In the past, the mutinies at Yunzhong and Baixia (Nanjing) made people wring their hands in anguish just to speak of them—how can such flames be allowed to blaze up again today? This is truly what is meant by "arrogant soldiers leaving behind calamity."

The cunning caitiffs are bold and voracious [?]. During the Jiajing (1522–1566) and Longqing (1567–1572) eras, the devastation of Huangfuchuan, the deep incursion at the Anding frontier fort, and the total annihilation of the army at Wazhaliang—how could all the circumstances of their rampant insolence be recounted even by changing servants! Although they have been tethered by peace settlements and tribute relations so that feathered urgent dispatches have somewhat abated, extortion and raids at the Jinglu gorge pass still occur repeatedly, Tibetan tribes are heavily plundered in Taozhou and Minzhou, and the distant frontier of Jiuquan is now swollen and peeled away…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
虜勢孤懸而莫之支矣誠所謂虜縱莫制
者額軍額餉舊有定衡但鹽鞔折於減派
實餽虧於增募侵年詘於取盈𤼵邊食矣
且也虜一歲市輒倍邀索貿劑如榷賈强
括如探囊其何厭之有如是不仰給
內帑卒無爲計誠所謂財苦不足者近自順
義物故虜心未一雖貢市如常而陽順陰
逆且牧且掠譎謀叵測知者睹未形矣已
著乎諸將固嬉然燕雀下也漫弗爲備惟
===
思所㣙之虜或薄吾軍至敗衄不可制方
縮慄斂避謂款市在也惟覬朝夕移旃去
耳孰有敢㒒然奮臂一當虜者迺有私寵
之麓蓑多於對壘之旌旄土築之畚鍤盛
於溢塞之戈甲卒不調習見豺而戰器不
精利執冰而踞例辦諸索復歲削月朘如
故假令一當虜猶投牂於餓虎之蹊即糜
之盡必無幸者夫虜以款市邀我我終以
款市亡備何無筭也爲今之策可膠執無
punctuated: 虜，勢孤懸而莫之支矣。誠所謂虜縱莫制者。額軍額餉，舊有定衡，但鹽鞔折於減派，實餽虧於增募，侵年詘於取盈，𤼵邊食矣。且也虜一歲市，輒倍邀索，貿劑如榷賈，强括如探囊，其何厭之有？如是不仰給內帑，卒無爲計。誠所謂財苦不足者。近自順義物故，虜心未一，雖貢市如常，而陽順陰逆，且牧且掠，譎謀叵測。知者睹未形，矣已著乎？諸將固嬉然燕雀下也，漫弗爲備，惟思所㣙之。虜或薄吾軍，至敗衄不可制，方縮慄斂避，謂款市在也，惟覬朝夕移旃去耳。孰有敢㒒然奮臂一當虜者？迺有私寵之麓蓑，多於對壘之旌旄；土築之畚鍤，盛於溢塞之戈甲。卒不調習，見豺而戰；器不精利，執冰而踞。例辦諸索，復歲削月朘如故。假令一當虜，猶投牂於餓虎之蹊，即糜之盡，必無幸者。夫虜以款市邀我，我終以款市亡備，何無筭也！爲今之策，可膠執無
translation_en:
… [the border], so our position hangs isolated and cannot be sustained. This is truly what is meant by the enemy running rampant beyond control.

Regular troop quotas and ration quotas formerly had fixed standards. However, the salt-exchange system and leather supplies [?] have been curtailed through reduced assessments, actual provisions have fallen short due to increased recruitment, and bad harvests have made it impossible to collect the full amounts, thus ruining [?] the frontier food supply. Moreover, each year when the caitiffs come to the border markets, they demand double the usual rewards; they haggle over tallies like monopolistic merchants and extort goods as easily as reaching into a bag—how could they ever be satisfied? Under such circumstances, if we do not rely on grants from the Inner Treasury, there is ultimately no way to manage. This is truly what is meant by suffering from an insufficiency of funds.

Recently, since the death of the Shunyi Prince (Altan Khan), the minds of the caitiffs have not been united. Although tribute and horse markets continue as usual, they are outwardly compliant while inwardly rebellious, herding and plundering at the same time, their deceitful plots unfathomable. The wise perceive things before they take shape—how much more so when they are already manifest! Yet our generals remain heedlessly merry like swallows and sparrows nesting beneath a burning roof; they casually fail to make preparations, thinking only of how to appease [?] them. When the caitiffs press upon our troops, even to the point of unmanageable defeat and rout, the generals merely cower, tremble, and shrink back, saying that the peace agreement and markets are still in effect, hoping only that the enemy will pack up their felt tents and depart from one day to the next. Who among them dares to rise up boldly and bare his arms to confront the caitiffs?

Instead, the bamboo baskets and straw raincoats used for private favors outnumber the banners and standards arrayed on the ramparts; the baskets and spades used for earthworks are more numerous than the spears and armor filling the frontier passes. The soldiers are untrained and tremble at the sight of a jackal; their weapons are neither fine nor sharp, so holding them is like gripping melting ice. Meanwhile, routine levies and various exactions continue to pare and fleece them month after month and year after year just as before. Suppose they were once to face the caitiffs: it would be like casting a ewe onto the path of a starving tiger—even if pulverized to the last man, none could hope to survive. Now, the caitiffs use the peace settlement and markets to coerce us, and in the end we abandon our defenses because of that very peace settlement and those markets—how utterly lacking in calculation! In devising a strategy for today, how can we cling stubbornly without…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
更解耶德威明信則戍卒無敢羣譁而彈
壓行戰守戒嚴則梟獍無敢過邀而漁索
節人有怖死之心而篤言乎貢市其誰與
戰則礪首功之賞捐啓釁之罪所當先也
則錄血戰之績貸損傷之失所當申也通
人稔蓄縮之習而首鼠乎損傷其誰與戰
丁多抱奇氣劒俠徂歲出絕漠擣巢趕馬
寔藉其死綏力繼以不任版築悉解體逋
亡去則汰老羸以收養武勇者非爲緩急
===
備耶番族徼福內屬星屯近寓固不侵不
叛之臣也黠虜鳩衆橫劫之胥歸詛盟聽
約束如驕醜嗚鏑不逞則肘腋之下皆貙
貐矣奚以厝手夫虜入熟番將傾覲望失
策者罪與內地同例甚嚴也獨不可振飭
之乎緩頰而哆談者此其大都也如選將
練兵秉塞罷役所覶縷者不與焉嗚乎套
虜舊列河外延慶不列亭障其來遠矣朔
方固無釁也成化歲火篩入套竊據竟至
punctuated:
更解耶？德威明信，則戍卒無敢羣譁，而彈壓行；戰守戒嚴，則梟獍無敢過邀，而漁索節。人有怖死之心，而篤言乎貢市，其誰與戰？則礪首功之賞，捐啓釁之罪，所當先也。則錄血戰之績，貸損傷之失，所當申也。通人稔蓄縮之習，而首鼠乎損傷，其誰與戰？丁多抱奇氣、劒俠，徂歲出絕漠，擣巢趕馬，寔藉其死綏力；繼以不任版築，悉解體逋亡去。則汰老羸以收養武勇者，非爲緩急備耶？番族徼福內屬，星屯近寓，固不侵不叛之臣也。黠虜鳩衆橫劫之，胥歸詛盟，聽約束。如驕醜嗚鏑不逞，則肘腋之下皆貙貐矣，奚以厝手？夫虜入熟番，將傾覲望，失策者罪與內地同，例甚嚴也，獨不可振飭之乎？緩頰而哆談者，此其大都也；如選將、練兵、秉塞、罷役，所覶縷者不與焉。

嗚乎！套虜舊列河外，延、慶不列亭障，其來遠矣，朔方固無釁也。成化歲，火篩入套竊據，竟至
translation_en:
…tuning the strings anew? When virtue and majesty are clearly trusted, the garrison soldiers will not dare to raise collective uproars, and firm suppression will prevail; when offense and defense are strictly guarded, those fierce beasts will not dare to make excessive demands, and their rapacious exactions will be curbed. When men harbor a fear of death and speak earnestly only of tribute and horse markets, who then will fight? Thus, sharpening rewards for taking enemy heads and setting aside the crime of provoking border incidents is what ought to be put first; recording the merits of bloody battles and pardoning losses from casualties is what ought to be reiterated. [Note: the original print appears to have transposed two columns here.] When men are thoroughly steeped in the habit of shrinking back and hesitate in two minds over casualties, who then will fight? The irregular housemen (tongding [?]) mostly possess extraordinary spirit and chivalrous swordsmanship; in past years, going out across the distant desert to raid enemy lairs and drive off their horses truly relied on their strength to fight to the death. Later, because they could not bear the labor of rammed-earth construction, they all lost heart, deserted, and fled. Is not weeding out the old and weak in order to recruit and support the martial and brave a way to prepare for emergencies? The Tibetan tribes (Fan) seek blessings by submitting to our rule, quartered like stars across the nearby borderlands; they are truly subjects who neither invade nor rebel. Yet the cunning caitiffs gather their multitudes to violently plunder them, so that all of them turn to swearing oaths of alliance with the enemy and obeying their terms. If those arrogant wretches sound their whistling arrows in unruly raids, then right beneath our elbows and armpits all will be fierce beasts of prey—how could we even lift a hand? Now, when the caitiffs invade the assimilated Tibetan tribes and our commanders lean back waiting and watching, those who fail in strategy are punished the same as for losses in the interior—the statute is very strict! Can we not rouse and rectify them? What loose-jawed and grandiloquent talkers speak of is, in the main, this; as for choosing generals, training troops, holding the passes, and halting corvée labor—things often detailed at length—they are not included here.

Alas! The Ordos caitiffs (Taolu) formerly ranged outside the Yellow River, and Yan'an and Qingyang did not set up frontier forts; this had been so for a long time, and the northern frontier (Shuofang) indeed had no rifts. In the Chenghua period (1465–1487), Huosai [note: anachronistic or generic reference to early Ordos chieftains/HuoShai] entered the Ordos Bend and usurped control of it, eventually leading to…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
釀骫不已文達肖𢇁套之議阻於因循維
揚肩驅埽之功格於怠遽籌惟今昔之邊
計輙掩卷有餘慨焉茲朔方部虜偪鄰塞
嗟哉我
國家自開平之棄則遼左不接上谷自興和
之徙則獨石不達雲中東勝不守即晉雲
遠隔賀蘭是豈朝夕故哉今固憂其漸也
戰可忘兵可弛也乎哉軍旅之事迺譚者
悉經生語顧何以仰副
明問
punctuated: 釀骫不已。文達肖𢇁套之議，阻於因循；維揚肩驅埽之功，格於怠遽。籌惟今昔之邊計，輙掩卷有餘慨焉。茲朔方部虜偪鄰塞，嗟哉！我國家自開平之棄，則遼左不接上谷；自興和之徙，則獨石不達雲中；東勝不守，即晉、雲遠隔賀蘭。是豈朝夕故哉？今固憂其漸也，戰可忘、兵可弛也乎哉？軍旅之事，迺譚者悉經生語，顧何以仰副明問？
translation_en: … fermenting crooked disorder without cease. Wenda's (Li Xian 李賢) proposal to clearsweep [?] the Ordos Loop was thwarted by adherence to routine, and Weiyang's (Zeng Xian 曾銑) undertaking of the meritorious task of driving them out and sweeping them away was blocked by negligence and haste. Whenever I ponder the border strategies of past and present, I always close the book with lingering sighs of regret. Now the caitiff tribes in the northern regions press close upon our neighboring frontiers—alas! In our state, ever since the abandonment of Kaiping, eastern Liaodong has lost contact with Shanggu; ever since the relocation from Xinghe, Dushi has no longer reached Yunzhong; and with Dongsheng left unguarded, Shanxi and Yunzhong are far cut off from the Helan Mountains. How could this be the result of a single morning or evening? Today we truly worry about its gradual worsening—how then can warfare be forgotten, or military preparations be relaxed? In matters of military campaigns, however, what speakers utter is nothing more than the talk of classicist scholars; how then can this suffice to respectfully answer Your sagely inquiry?

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陜西鄉試錄後序
皇上御極之十年陜西例當貢士
〔有年〕以御史之辟典其事既
從諸文學掌故盡讀多士所
爲文則作而嘆曰嘻盛哉
聖世之化乎夫岐豳豐鎬豈非文
武成宣之舊哉自秦襄東徙
===
蒙周爲秦而其國風亦由二
南雅頌而爲小戎無衣蒹葭
諸什迺王國之生故所稱周
楨者亦浸假而爲伯佐爲力
臣未有師法周召而紹明言
甫諸臣之業者豈其風會使
然抑亦有所作之者與夫思
punctuated:
陜西鄉試錄後序

皇上御極之十年，陜西例當貢士，〔有年〕以御史之辟典其事。既從諸文學掌故，盡讀多士所爲文，則作而嘆曰：嘻，盛哉，聖世之化乎！夫岐、豳、豐、鎬，豈非文、武、成、宣之舊哉？自秦襄東徙，蒙周爲秦，而其國風亦由二南、雅、頌而爲《小戎》、《無衣》、《蒹葭》諸什；迺王國之生，故所稱「周楨」者，亦浸假而爲伯佐、爲力臣，未有師法周、召而紹明言、甫諸臣之業者。豈其風會使然，抑亦有所作之者與？夫思
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the tenth year of His Majesty's reign (1582), Shaanxi was scheduled by precedent to present tribute scholars, and I, [Younian], having been summoned by the Censor, took charge of the affair. After joining the various classicists and erudites in reading through all the essays composed by the many scholars, I rose and sighed, saying: Ah, how flourishing is the transformative influence of our sacred age! Are not Qi, Bin, Feng, and Hao the old territories of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Xuan? Ever since Duke Xiang of Qin moved eastward, superseding Zhou to become Qin, the airs of the state likewise shifted from the Two Nan, the Odes (Ya), and the Hymns (Song) to become pieces such as "Lesser War Chariot" (Xiaorong), "No Clothes" (Wuyi), and "Reeds and Rushes" (Jianjia). And the men born of the royal domain—those once hailed as the "pillars of Zhou"—also gradually turned into aides to hegemons and ministers of brute force, with none taking the Dukes of Zhou and Shao as their models or carrying forward and illuminating the achievements of ministers like Yan [Yin Jifu?] and Zhongshan Fu. Was this brought about by the prevailing ethos of the times, or was there someone who instigated it? Now, to be pensive…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
而不貳曲而有直體周聲也
追琢其章金玉其相周德也
迺玆多士勁氣和衷繁響急
節無復粗厲猛起要已近之
其所稱引理道剽剝王伯無
論鞅儀起翦即百里孟明西
乞術之流不能自解免又若
===
遡游吉甫諸臣以遡洄周召
者秦之士與夫非秦之士與
何其聲之不爲秦也夫有文
武成宣之君則有菁莪棫樸
之化有其化矣而後有馮翼
孝德之材有其材矣而後有
肆好孔碩之聲其作之誠有
punctuated: 而不貳，曲而有直體，周聲也；追琢其章，金玉其相，周德也。迺玆多士，勁氣和衷，繁響急節，無復粗厲猛起，要已近之。其所稱引理道，剽剝王伯，無論鞅、儀、起、翦，即百里、孟明、西乞術之流，不能自解免；又若遡游吉甫諸臣，以遡洄周、召者。秦之士與？夫非秦之士與？何其聲之不爲秦也！夫有文、武、成、宣之君，則有《菁莪》、《棫樸》之化；有其化矣，而後有馮翼孝德之材；有其材矣，而後有肆好孔碩之聲。其作之誠有
translation_en: …without duplicity, and winding yet maintaining an upright form—such was the sound of Zhou. Carving and polishing its outward pattern, with gold and jade as its substance—such was the virtue of Zhou. Now, among this multitude of scholars, their vigorous spirit is matched by a harmonious mind, and their rich resonances and brisk rhythms no longer show coarse fierceness or sudden violence; in essence, they have already come close to it. In citing principles and the Way, and in dissecting the distinction between true kingship and hegemony, not to mention Shang Yang 商鞅, Zhang Yi 張儀, Bai Qi 白起, and Wang Jian 王翦, even the likes of Baili Xi 百里奚, Mengming Shi 孟明視, and Xiqv Shu 西乞術 cannot excuse themselves; and it is as if they are swimming with the current back to Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 and other ministers, and against the current all the way back to the Duke of Zhou 周公 and the Duke of Shao 召公. Are they scholars of Qin? Or are they not scholars of Qin? Why is it that their voice is not that of Qin! Now, when there are rulers like Kings Wen 文王, Wu 武王, Cheng 成王, and Xuan 宣王, then there is the transformative influence celebrated in the odes "Jing'e" (Lush Wormwood) and "Yupu" (Thickets of Oak); once there is that transformative influence, there are talents of supportive wing-like assistance and filial virtue; and once there are such talents, there are voices that are grand, fine, and exceedingly great. That which inspires and rouses them truly has…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
自也惟我
祖宗道化翔洽海宇惟我
皇上紹統覲揚而光大之
壽考作人於是乎始基之矣其所
揚詡訢合郎椎結雕膂之流
且有釋傑僑而佔俾弦誦者
矧茲多士生周之邦涵泳於
===
聖世繼周之化者乎昔季札之歌
秦曰此之謂夏聲又曰其周
之舊夫以周之舊流而爲秦
是秦之過也迺今以秦之風
遡而之乎二千年有周之舊
非
聖世道化其孰與成之夫秦且爲
punctuated: 自也。惟我祖宗道化翔洽海宇，惟我皇上紹統覲揚而光大之，壽考作人，於是乎始基之矣。其所揚詡訢合，郎椎結雕膂之流，且有釋傑僑而佔俾弦誦者，矧茲多士生周之邦、涵泳於聖世繼周之化者乎？昔季札之歌《秦》曰：「此之謂夏聲。」又曰：「其周之舊。」夫以周之舊流而爲秦，是秦之過也；迺今以秦之風遡而之乎二千年有周之舊，非聖世道化，其孰與成之？夫秦且爲
translation_en: …its source. Truly, the moral transformation of our Imperial Ancestors has soared across and pervaded the whole realm, and our Reigning Emperor has inherited the succession, manifestly exalting and glorifying it; the work of "living long and cultivating men" has thus established its foundation right here. Through that which it extols and harmonizes, even those [?; 郎 for 即] of the sort who wear mallet-shaped topknots and tattoo their bodies cast aside their unruly arrogance [?; 傑僑 for 桀驁] to pore over texts and chant to stringed instruments—how much more so these many scholars, who were born in the old lands of Zhou and have been steeped in a sacred age's moral transformation that continues the legacy of Zhou! In antiquity, when Jizha 季札 heard the songs of Qin, he said: "This is what is called the sound of Xia." And he also said: "Perhaps they are the old airs of Zhou." Now, that the old traditions of Zhou degenerated to become Qin was the fault of Qin; yet today, to trace back from the customs of Qin and return to the two-thousand-year-old traditions of the house of Zhou—if not for the moral transformation of this sacred age, what else could have brought this to completion? Now, if the airs of Qin are on the verge of becoming…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
二南風且爲雅頌抑何疑於
士之不爲周乎〔有年〕是以重
有感於
聖化也士既錄有司者歌鹿鳴諸
什以燕樂之御史謂周行之
義〔有年〕亦當有言〔有年〕乃言
曰古者諸侯采詩以貢於天
===
子天子納其貢則命太師領
之今采詩之貢不行而錄士
以文是文也彬彬乎追琢之
章矣可以貢矣抑亦有金玉
其相者乎未可知也洛爾多
士著之心聲嗣響周雅主司
業已周士期之矣無言周召
punctuated: 《二南》，《風》且爲《雅》、《頌》，抑何疑於士之不爲周乎？〔有年〕是以重有感於聖化也。士既錄，有司者歌《鹿鳴》諸什以燕樂之。御史謂「周行」之義，〔有年〕亦當有言。〔有年〕乃言曰：古者諸侯采詩以貢於天子，天子納其貢，則命太師領之。今采詩之貢不行，而錄士以文。是文也，彬彬乎追琢之章矣，可以貢矣！抑亦有「金玉其相」者乎？未可知也。洛爾多士，著之心聲，嗣響《周雅》，主司業已周士期之矣。無言周、召，
translation_en:
… the Two Nan (Ernan), and the Airs (Feng) will furthermore become the Odes (Ya) and Hymns (Song)—then why doubt that the scholars will become like those of Zhou? Because of this, I, Younian, am deeply moved by the sacred transformation.

Once the scholars had been selected and recorded, the authorities sang the "Deer Cry" (Luming) and other odes to feast and entertain them. The Censor said that regarding the meaning of the "Great Way" (zhouhang, from the "Deer Cry" ode), I, Younian, ought also to offer some words. I, Younian, thereupon said: In antiquity, the feudal lords collected poems to present as tribute to the Son of Heaven; the Son of Heaven accepted their tribute and ordered the Grand Music Master (Taishi) to take charge of them. Today, the tribute of collecting poems is no longer practiced; instead, scholars are selected and recorded on the basis of their essays. These essays are refined indeed, like carved and polished ornaments ("zhuizhuo zhi zhang," Book of Odes, "Yu Pu"), and are worthy of being presented as tribute! Yet are there also those among them whose inner substance is of gold and jade ("jinyu qi xiang")? That cannot yet be known. Ah [? 洛, likely a carving error for 咨], you many scholars! What you have set forth as the voices of your hearts echoes as successor to the Odes of Zhou (Zhou ya), and the examiners have already placed their expectations in you as scholars of Zhou. Not to speak of the Dukes of Zhou and Shao,…

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
抑亦有吉甫其人者乎未可
知也夫穆如清風共武服而
定王國吉甫所以萬邦爲憲
也爾多士信有是焉異日者
矢其肆好孔碩而攄其馮翼
孝德以我
國家匹休文武成宣而收其菁
===
義棫樸之效允哉其爲周士
矣萬有一者挾持浮說而非
其質揣之無當措之用而罔
效則聲猶周也吾意不若爲
秦何者彼信粗厲猛起而兼
葭之果於從人小戎無衣之
勇於赴義猶其質也
punctuated: 抑亦有吉甫其人者乎？未可知也。夫「穆如清風」，「共武服」而「定王國」，吉甫所以「萬邦爲憲」也。爾多士信有是焉，異日者矢其「肆好」「孔碩」，而攄其「馮翼孝德」，以我國家匹休文、武、成、宣，而收其「菁義」「棫樸」之效，允哉其爲周士矣！萬有一者挾持浮說而非其質，揣之無當，措之用而罔效，則聲猶周也，吾意不若爲秦。何者？彼信粗厲猛起，而《兼葭》之果於從人，《小戎》、《無衣》之勇於赴義，猶其質也。
translation_en:
…or are there even men such as Yin Jifu 尹吉甫 among them? That cannot yet be known. Now, creating verses "gentle as the clear wind," "reverently attending to military service," and "stabilizing the royal kingdom"—this was how Jifu "became a model for the myriad states." If you many scholars truly possess these qualities, on some future day you will set forth works "grand and fine" and "exceedingly great," and display your "supportive and filial virtue," so that our Dynasty may match the glorious blessings of Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Xuan of Zhou, and reap the results celebrated in the odes "Luxuriant Southernwood" (Jingyi 菁莪 [transcribed 菁義?]) and "Dense Scrub-Oak" (Yupu 棫樸). Truly, you will be scholars of the Zhou!

Should there be one in ten thousand who clings to superficial talk devoid of genuine substance—measuring up to nothing when examined, and yielding no results when put to practical use—then even though his voice sounds like that of Zhou, in my view he is not even as good as a man of Qin. Why is that? Though the people of Qin were indeed rough, fierce, and impetuous, the resoluteness in seeking the worthy man shown in the ode "Reeds and Rushes" (Jianjia 蒹葭 [transcribed 兼葭]), and the courage in rushing to a righteous cause shown in the odes "Small War Chariot" (Xiaorong 小戎) and "No Clothes" (Wuyi 無衣), at least possessed genuine substance. …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
國家取士參合成周辨論官材
必按其藝而考其德行之實
故清廟之樂依於和且平者
而繁哇必删治世之材貴於
端且碩者而浮詭必絀彼靜
言庸違文飭用寡登進者右
之辨論者左之後之人且指
===
是錄而姍之曰秦無人錄有
餘辱矣又何敢望周之下隷
乎〔有年〕爲此懼故爲是過計
以告多士多士勗哉無負主
司尚亦無負
聖世之化也哉
四川順慶府西充縣儒學敎
punctuated:
國家取士，參合成周辨論官材，必按其藝而考其德行之實。故清廟之樂，依於和且平者，而繁哇必删；治世之材，貴於端且碩者，而浮詭必絀。彼靜言庸違、文飭用寡，登進者右之，辨論者左之。後之人且指是錄而姍之曰：「秦無人，錄有餘辱矣！」又何敢望周之下隷乎？〔有年〕爲此懼，故爲是過計以告多士。多士勗哉！無負主司，尚亦無負聖世之化也哉！
四川順慶府西充縣儒學敎
translation_en:
In selecting scholars, the dynasty incorporates the perfection of the Zhou in evaluating and discussing candidates for office, always examining their literary craft while investigating the reality of their moral conduct. Therefore, the music of the ancestral temple relies on what is harmonious and balanced, while ornate and licentious tunes must be expunged; the talents of a well-governed age are valued for being upright and substantial, while superficial and deceitful ones must be dismissed. As for those who speak smoothly when idle yet act perversely when employed, whose literary polish offers scant practical utility: even if those who promote them favor them, those who evaluate them for office will demote them. Men of later generations will point to this record and mock it, saying: "There were no true men in Qin; this record has brought more than enough disgrace!" How then could they dare hope to match even the lowest menials of the Zhou? I, Younian, fear this, and so I have offered these overly anxious words to admonish the many scholars. Take heed, you scholars! Do not fail the chief examiners, and still more, do not fail the civilizing transformation of this sacred age!

[Instructor] of the Confucian School of Xichong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan …

title: 萬曆十年陝西鄉試錄
text:
諭田〔有年〕謹序
===
是錄后
punctuated:
諭田〔有年〕謹序。
===
是錄后。
translation_en:
…Instructor Tian Younian 田有年 respectfully writes this preface.

End of this Record.
